#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build, install, receive and preserve the complete original CanadaBuys customer workflow."""
from __future__ import annotations
import ast,contextlib,fcntl,hashlib,json,os,select,shutil,signal,stat,subprocess,sys,time,traceback,uuid,zipfile
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime,timezone

OP="CANADABUYS-INSTALLED-INTAKE-6BA15-20261013"
ROOT=Path("/dev/canadabuys-installed-intake-6ba15-20261013")
SHARED=Path("/workspace/scratch/6ba15c52ace4/canadabuys-intake-delivery-20261013")
OWNED=None
def now():return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
def encoded(value):return (json.dumps(value,sort_keys=True,separators=(",",":"),ensure_ascii=False)+"\n").encode()
def sha(raw):return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
def require(value,message):
 if not value:raise RuntimeError(message)
def emit(event_name,**values):print(json.dumps({"event":event_name,"operationId":OP,"at":now(),**values},separators=(",",":")),flush=True)
def private(path):
 path=Path(path);path.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True,mode=0o700)
 require(not path.is_symlink() and path.is_dir() and path.resolve()==path,"Expected a canonical owned directory: "+str(path))
 os.chmod(path,0o700);return path
def record(path):
 path=Path(path);handle=os.open(path,os.O_RDONLY|os.O_NOFOLLOW)
 try:
  before=os.fstat(handle);require(stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode),"Expected a regular original file")
  digest=hashlib.sha256();size=0
  while True:
   block=os.read(handle,1048576)
   if not block:break
   size+=len(block);digest.update(block)
  after=os.fstat(handle);named=path.lstat()
  require((before.st_dev,before.st_ino,before.st_size,before.st_mtime_ns)==(after.st_dev,after.st_ino,after.st_size,after.st_mtime_ns)
          and (named.st_dev,named.st_ino)==(before.st_dev,before.st_ino) and size==before.st_size,"Original file changed while read")
  return {"path":str(path),"bytes":size,"sha256":digest.hexdigest()}
 finally:os.close(handle)
def syncdir(path):
 fd=os.open(path,os.O_RDONLY|os.O_DIRECTORY)
 try:os.fsync(fd)
 finally:os.close(fd)
def publish(path,raw):
 path=Path(path);private(path.parent)
 if path.exists():
  selected=record(path);require(selected["bytes"]==len(raw) and selected["sha256"]==sha(raw),"Original immutable file differs: "+str(path));return path
 temporary=path.with_name("."+path.name+"."+uuid.uuid4().hex+".tmp")
 fd=os.open(temporary,os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL|os.O_NOFOLLOW,0o600)
 try:
  with os.fdopen(fd,"wb",closefd=False) as stream:stream.write(raw);stream.flush();os.fsync(fd)
 finally:os.close(fd)
 try:
  try:os.link(temporary,path)
  except FileExistsError:require(record(path)["sha256"]==sha(raw),"Concurrent immutable file differs")
  syncdir(path.parent)
 finally:temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

def pubjson(path,value):return publish(path,encoded(value))
def readjson(path):return json.loads(Path(path).read_bytes())
def same(expected,path):
 actual=record(path);require(actual==expected,"Original exact file descriptor differs: "+str(path));return actual
def copy_exact(source,destination,expected):
 source=Path(source);destination=Path(destination);same(expected,source);private(destination.parent)
 if destination.exists():
  selected=record(destination);require(selected["bytes"]==expected["bytes"] and selected["sha256"]==expected["sha256"],"Staged original file differs");return destination
 temporary=destination.with_name("."+destination.name+"."+uuid.uuid4().hex+".copy")
 with source.open("rb") as inp,temporary.open("xb") as out:
  os.chmod(temporary,0o600);shutil.copyfileobj(inp,out,1048576);out.flush();os.fsync(out.fileno())
 try:
  selected=record(temporary);require(selected["bytes"]==expected["bytes"] and selected["sha256"]==expected["sha256"],"Complete staging copy differs")
  os.link(temporary,destination);syncdir(destination.parent)
 finally:temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
 same(expected,source);return destination
def finish_saved_artifact(path,kept,reused):
 raise RuntimeError("This operation uses its current supported Library tool receipt")
def save_artifact(path):raise RuntimeError("The supported Library bridge is not installed")
def observation():
 raw=Path("/proc/self/stat").read_text();end=raw.rfind(")");f=raw[end+2:].split()
 return {"pid":int(raw.split("(",1)[0].strip()),"startTicks":f[19],"bootId":Path("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id").read_text().strip(),"namespacePid":os.getpid()}
def inactive(selected):
 if selected["bootId"]!=Path("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id").read_text().strip():return True
 try:raw=Path("/proc")/str(selected["pid"])/"stat";text=raw.read_text()
 except FileNotFoundError:return True
 f=text[text.rfind(")")+2:].split()

def resource():
 value={"observer":observation()}
 for name in ("memory.current","memory.max","memory.peak","memory.events"):
  try:value[name]=Path("/sys/fs/cgroup",name).read_text().strip()
  except OSError as error:value[name]={"errno":error.errno}

def stop_child(child):
 if child is None or child.poll() is not None:return

 try:child.wait(timeout=10)

  with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):os.killpg(child.pid,signal.SIGKILL)
  child.wait(timeout=10)
def run_command(label,argv,environment,timeout=1800):
 global OWNED
 directory=private(ROOT/"commands"/label)
 request={"schema":"commons.canadabuys-customer-command.v1","operationId":OP,"label":label,"argv":argv,"sourceCommit":PAYLOAD["sourceCommit"]}
 request_path=pubjson(directory/"request.json",request);request_hash=record(request_path)["sha256"]

  old=readjson(completed);require(old["requestSha256"]==request_hash and old["exitCode"]==0,"Original completed command differs")
  same(old["stdout"],Path(old["stdout"]["path"]));same(old["stderr"],Path(old["stderr"]["path"]));emit("COMMAND_REUSED",label=label);return old
 for intent in sorted(directory.glob("*.intent.json")):
  original=readjson(intent);require(original["requestSha256"]==request_hash,"Original command intent differs")
  prefix=intent.name[:-len(".intent.json")]
  process_path=directory/(prefix+".process.json");result_path=directory/(prefix+".result.json")
  require(process_path.exists(),"An original command intent has no resolved acquired-child receipt")
  process_record=readjson(process_path)
  require(process_record["requestSha256"]==request_hash and inactive(process_record["process"]),"An original acquired command remains active")
  require(result_path.exists(),"The original command has no terminal receipt; reconcile that same command before continuing")
  previous=readjson(result_path)
  require(previous["requestSha256"]==request_hash and previous["process"]==process_record["process"],"Original terminal command binding differs")
  same(previous["stdout"],Path(previous["stdout"]["path"]));same(previous["stderr"],Path(previous["stderr"]["path"]))
  if previous["exitCode"]==0:
   pubjson(completed,previous);emit("COMMAND_REUSED",label=label,reconciledTerminal=True);return previous
 attempt=uuid.uuid4().hex
 stdout=directory/(attempt+".stdout.log");stderr=directory/(attempt+".stderr.log")
 pubjson(directory/(attempt+".intent.json"),{"requestSha256":request_hash,"parent":observation(),"createdAt":now(),"resources":resource()})
 parent=observation();identity_r,identity_w=os.pipe();child=None
 with stdout.open("xb",buffering=0) as out,stderr.open("xb",buffering=0) as errors:
  os.chmod(stdout,0o600);os.chmod(stderr,0o600)
  try:
   child=subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,"-u",str(ROOT/"producer/child_gate.py"),str(request_path),str(identity_w)],
     stdin=subprocess.PIPE,stdout=out,stderr=errors,env=environment,start_new_session=True,pass_fds=(identity_w,),close_fds=True,cwd=str(ROOT))
   OWNED=child;os.close(identity_w);identity_w=None
   deadline=time.monotonic()+30;raw=bytearray()
   while True:
    remaining=deadline-time.monotonic();require(remaining>0,"Original child identity timed out")
    ready,_,_=select.select([identity_r],[],[],remaining);require(ready,"Original child identity unavailable")
    block=os.read(identity_r,4096)
    if not block:break
    raw.extend(block);require(len(raw)<16384,"Original child identity too large")
   selected=json.loads(raw);os.close(identity_r);identity_r=None
   require(selected["requestSha256"]==request_hash and selected["argv"]==argv and selected["namespacePid"]==child.pid
           and selected["parentHostPid"]==parent["pid"] and selected["process"]["bootId"]==parent["bootId"]
           and child.poll() is None,"Original acquired child identity differs")
   pubjson(directory/(attempt+".process.json"),selected)
   pubjson(directory/(attempt+".dispatch.json"),{"requestSha256":request_hash,"process":selected["process"],"releasedAt":now()})
   child.stdin.write(b"START\n");child.stdin.flush();child.stdin.close()
   emit("COMMAND_STARTED",label=label,process=selected["process"],namespacePid=child.pid,resources=resource())
   started=time.monotonic();position=0;pending=b""
   while child.poll() is None:
    require(time.monotonic()-started<timeout,"Original complete command exceeded its selected lifetime")
    with stdout.open("rb") as stream:stream.seek(position);block=stream.read(65536);position+=len(block)
    pending+=block
    while b"\n" in pending:
     line,pending=pending.split(b"\n",1)
     try:
      value=json.loads(line)
      if isinstance(value,dict) and value.get("event"):print(json.dumps(value,separators=(",",":")),flush=True)
     except (ValueError,UnicodeError):pass
    time.sleep(0.2)
   code=child.wait()
  except BaseException:
   stop_child(child);raise
  finally:
   for fd in (identity_r,identity_w):
    if fd is not None:
     with contextlib.suppress(OSError):os.close(fd)
   if child is not None and child.poll() is None:stop_child(child)
   OWNED=None;out.flush();errors.flush();os.fsync(out.fileno());os.fsync(errors.fileno())
 result={"schema":"commons.canadabuys-customer-command-result.v1","requestSha256":request_hash,"process":selected["process"],"exitCode":code,"completedAt":now(),"stdout":record(stdout),"stderr":record(stderr),"resources":resource()}
 pubjson(directory/(attempt+".result.json"),result)
 if code!=0:
  tail=stderr.read_text(errors="replace")[-12000:]
  emit("COMMAND_FAILED",label=label,exitCode=code,stderr=tail,stdout=str(stdout))
  raise RuntimeError("Original command "+label+" failed with exit "+str(code))
 pubjson(completed,result);emit("COMMAND_COMPLETE",label=label,exitCode=0);return result
def complete_archive(filename,kind):
 output=ROOT/"deliveries"/filename;private(output.parent)
 descriptor=output.with_suffix(output.suffix+".json")
 if output.exists():
  require(descriptor.exists(),"Original published archive receipt is absent; reconcile its bytes")
  receipt=readjson(descriptor);same(receipt["archive"],output);return output
 selected=[]
 for directory,names,files in os.walk(ROOT,followlinks=False):
  current=Path(directory)
  if current==ROOT/"deliveries":names[:]=[];continue
  names[:]=sorted(names)
  for name in sorted(files):
   file=current/name
   require(not file.is_symlink() and file.is_file(),"Portable source contains a linked or special file")
   selected.append({"path":file.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(),"file":file,**{k:v for k,v in record(file).items() if k!="path"}})
 manifest={"schema":"commons.canadabuys-customer-complete-delivery.v1","operationId":OP,"kind":kind,"sourceCommit":PAYLOAD["sourceCommit"],
           "files":[{k:v for k,v in row.items() if k!="file"} for row in selected]}
 raw=encoded(manifest);temporary=output.with_name("."+output.name+"."+uuid.uuid4().hex+".zip")
 with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary,"x",compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,compresslevel=6) as archive:
  for row in selected:
   before=record(row["file"]);require(before["bytes"]==row["bytes"] and before["sha256"]==row["sha256"],"Delivery source changed")
   archive.write(row["file"],row["path"]);same(before,row["file"])
  archive.writestr("DELIVERY_MEMBERS.json",raw)
 with temporary.open("rb") as handle:os.fsync(handle.fileno())
 with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary) as archive:
  require(len(archive.namelist())==len(selected)+1 and len(set(archive.namelist()))==len(selected)+1,"Complete archive inventory differs")
  for row in selected:
   with archive.open(row["path"]) as source:
    digest=hashlib.sha256();size=0
    while True:
     block=source.read(1048576)
     if not block:break
     digest.update(block);size+=len(block)
   require(size==row["bytes"] and digest.hexdigest()==row["sha256"],"Complete archive member differs")
 os.link(temporary,output);temporary.unlink();syncdir(output.parent)
 pubjson(descriptor,{"archive":record(output),"manifest":{"bytes":len(raw),"sha256":sha(raw)},"members":len(selected)+1,"kind":kind,"at":now()})
 emit("COMPLETE_ARCHIVE_VERIFIED",**record(output),members=len(selected)+1,kind=kind);return output
def main():
 global PAYLOAD
 PAYLOAD=NATIVE_INPUT
 private(ROOT);private(SHARED)
 lease=os.open(ROOT/"producer.lock",os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREAT|os.O_NOFOLLOW,0o600);fcntl.flock(lease,fcntl.LOCK_EX|fcntl.LOCK_NB)

  for item in PAYLOAD["sourceFiles"]:

   raw=item["content"].encode();require(len(raw)==item["bytes"] and sha(raw)==item["sha256"],"Full received source differs: "+name)
   path=publish(ROOT/"incoming-source"/name,raw);os.chmod(path,0o755 if item["mode"]=="100755" else 0o644)

"""Report the acquired child's own procfs identity before the parent's START."""
import hashlib,json,os,sys
from pathlib import Path
request_path=Path(sys.argv[1]);write_fd=int(sys.argv[2])
raw=request_path.read_bytes();request=json.loads(raw)
stat=Path("/proc/self/stat").read_text();end=stat.rfind(")");fields=stat[end+2:].split()
identity={"pid":int(stat.split("(",1)[0].strip()),"startTicks":fields[19],
          "bootId":Path("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id").read_text().strip()}
value={"process":identity,"parentHostPid":int(fields[1]),"namespacePid":os.getpid(),
       "requestSha256":hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),"argv":request["argv"]}
with os.fdopen(write_fd,"wb",buffering=0) as handle:
 handle.write((json.dumps(value,separators=(",",":"))+"\n").encode())
if sys.stdin.buffer.readline()!=b"START\n":raise RuntimeError("Original receiving child was not released")
os.execvpe(request["argv"][0],request["argv"],os.environ)

"""Supported Library tool transport reused from the observed Aviary save bridge.

This module contains only the original save event/reply transport and strict
observed-response validation. Artifact restoration remains with the caller.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
import sys

def library_name_matches(actual,requested):
 """Accept the original basename or Library's observed numbered collision name."""
 if not isinstance(actual,str) or Path(actual).name!=actual:return False
 if actual==requested:return True
 stem,suffix=os.path.splitext(requested)
 return re.fullmatch(re.escape(stem)+r"\([1-9][0-9]*\)"+re.escape(suffix),actual) is not None

def install_original_library_tool_bridge(n):
 original_finish=n["finish_saved_artifact"]
 def finish(path,kept,reused):
  if kept.get("transferSourceKind")!="official-library-local-file":
   return original_finish(path,kept,reused)
  rec=n["record"](path);n["require"](kept["source"]==rec,"Original official saved artifact bytes differ")
  evidence=Path(kept["officialToolEvidence"]["path"])
  n["require"](evidence==n["ROOT"]/"library-tool-receipts"/(Path(path).name+".response.json"),"Original official receipt path differs")
  normalized_result(kept["providerReceipt"],Path(path).name,rec["bytes"])
  raw=n["encoded"](kept["providerReceipt"])
  n["require"](len(raw)==kept["officialToolEvidence"]["bytes"] and n["sha"](raw)==kept["officialToolEvidence"]["sha256"],"Retained original official response bytes differ")
  n["publish"](evidence,raw);n["same"](kept["officialToolEvidence"],evidence)
  item=kept["result"]
  n["require"](item["local_path"]==str(path) and item["purpose"]=="create_library_file"
               and item["status"]=="succeeded" and item["file_id"] and item["library_file_id"],
               "Original official save receipt is incomplete")
  n["emit"]("ARTIFACT_SAVED",**item,bytes=rec["bytes"],sha256=rec["sha256"],reused=reused)
  n["pubjson"](n["SHARED"]/"receipts"/(Path(path).name+".json"),kept)
  return kept
 def read_command():
  line=bytearray()
  while not line.endswith(b"\n"):
   block=os.read(sys.stdin.fileno(),1)
   n["require"](block,"Official save reply input ended before its original receipt")
   line.extend(block);n["require"](len(line)<=2000000,"Official save reply exceeds its bound")
  return json.loads(line)
 def normalized_result(raw,name,size):
  n["require"](isinstance(raw,dict) and raw.get("isError") is False,"Official Library tool did not return success")
  item=raw.get("structuredContent")
  n["require"](isinstance(item,dict) and item.get("operation")=="create_library_file"
      and item.get("status")=="succeeded" and library_name_matches(item.get("file_name"),name)
      and item.get("file_size_bytes")==size and isinstance(item.get("file_id"),str)
      and item["file_id"].startswith("file_") and isinstance(item.get("library_file_id"),str)
      and item["library_file_id"].startswith("libfile_")
      and type(item.get("current_version_number")) is int,
      "Official Library returned identity/name/size/version does not match the exact staged artifact")
  return item
 def save(path):
  path=Path(path);rec=n["record"](path);name=path.name
  folder=n["ROOT"]/"library-receipts";folder.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True,mode=0o700)
  journal=folder/(name+".json")
  if journal.exists():return finish(path,n["readjson"](journal),True)
  n["require"](not (folder/(name+".attempt.json")).exists(),"An original canonical upload remains unresolved; official save was not dispatched")
  bridge_root=n["ROOT"]/"library-tool-receipts";bridge_root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True,mode=0o700)
  stage=n["SHARED"]/"official-save-source"/name
  n["copy_exact"](path,stage,rec);stage_rec=n["record"](stage)
  request={"schema":"commons.aviary.official-library-local-save.v1","operation":n["OP"],
           "tool":"library_create_library_file","source":rec,"staged":stage_rec,
           "arguments":{"file":str(stage),"library_artifact_type":"other"}}
  request_sha=n["sha"](n["encoded"](request))
  intent=bridge_root/(name+".request.json");response=bridge_root/(name+".response.json")
  reused=intent.exists()
  if reused:
   n["require"](n["readjson"](intent)==request,"The retained official save request differs")
   n["require"](response.is_file(),"The original official save is unresolved; no duplicate save was requested")
  else:
   n["pubjson"](intent,request)
   n["emit"]("LIBRARY_SAVE_REQUEST",requestSha256=request_sha,name=name,source=rec,staged=stage_rec,
             arguments=request["arguments"],requestEvidence=n["record"](intent))
   command=read_command()
   n["require"](command.get("action")=="official-library-save-result" and command.get("requestSha256")==request_sha,
                "Official Library reply belongs to another original artifact")
   n["pubjson"](response,command["result"])
  raw=n["readjson"](response);selected=normalized_result(raw,name,rec["bytes"])
  n["same"](rec,path);n["same"](stage_rec,stage)
  xattrs=selected.get("xattrs",[])
  applied=[]
  for item in xattrs:
   if not isinstance(item,dict) or not isinstance(item.get("name"),str) or not isinstance(item.get("value"),str):continue
   for target in (path,stage):
    try:os.setxattr(target,item["name"],item["value"].encode());applied.append({"path":str(target),"name":item["name"],"applied":True})
    except OSError as error:applied.append({"path":str(target),"name":item["name"],"applied":False,"errno":error.errno})
  item={"local_path":str(path),"purpose":"create_library_file","status":"succeeded",
        "file_id":selected["file_id"],"library_file_id":selected["library_file_id"],"file_name":selected["file_name"],
        "current_version_number":selected.get("current_version_number",selected.get("version_number")),
        "local_metadata_applied":bool(applied) and all(x["applied"] for x in applied)}
  kept={"source":rec,"staged":stage_rec,"transferSourceKind":"official-library-local-file",
        "providerReceipt":raw,"officialToolEvidence":n["record"](response),
        "originalRequest":n["record"](intent),"result":item,"saved":n["now"](),
        "responseReconciled":reused,"xattrs":applied,
        "verification":"Supported library_create_library_file result, complete original response and exact private/staged bytes"}
  n["pubjson"](journal,kept);return finish(path,kept,reused)

# CanadaBuys saved bidder desk

The bidder desk turns the existing retained CanadaBuys notices into a saved company review and decision workflow. It uses the original SQLite workspace, original source rows, HTTP service, Applications lifecycle, client, CLI, merchant provider and package receiver.

Open **Bidder desk** from the procurement workspace. The direct local route is **/bidder-desk**. The application remains a single owned local service. Its two browser pages use the same workspace.

## Operating journey

### 1. Select the company and actual opportunity

Capture or import the complete official tender source in the procurement workspace. The bidder page lists its retained notices; search by title, buyer or reference. The selected notice shows the original reference and solicitation numbers, publisher status, original closing field, source capture, complete bilingual row, linked documents and all retained editions.

Create a company profile under **Company profile**. Save its legal and operating names, capabilities, included/excluded terms, procurement categories, exact commodity code families, delivery/opportunity regions, qualification claims and supporting documents. Capacity separates delivery availability from minimum bid preparation time. Commercial preferences retain exact decimal amounts and currency; blank values remain unspecified.

The company profile is an authored statement. A matching keyword or commodity code is a reason to inspect the opportunity. The fit result exposes each observed publisher value, the declared capability and the reason for a match, gap or unknown. The human decision is saved separately.

**Check profile fit** evaluates every retained notice against the selected saved profile. **Review this notice against the selected profile** opens all checks for the current notice. Each result includes the exact source entry, source-row hash and selected profile revision.

### 2. Retain and review the documents

Under **Documents**, save the solicitation and its amendments, annexes, questions and answers, supplier records, certifications, security documents and past-performance evidence. Select the original source URL, publisher version, issue date, relevant page/section and relationship to any earlier document.

Attach the actual file to retain its complete bytes. Browser, client and native model enforce a 64 MiB per-document capacity. The model calculates the digest and byte length, retains the body once per digest and keeps each document metadata edition. Downloading an earlier document revision returns its original body.

A document may instead retain a link, an access restriction or a retrieval failure. These states remain visible. Mark the document **REVIEWED** with reviewer, review time and note when its content has been reviewed. A company document can be shared across notices; a solicitation document remains bound to its original notice.

Replacing document bytes, source URL, version, issue date or access state produces a new edition. A material change resets review to **UNREVIEWED** unless the submitted edit includes an explicit new review with reviewer and a later review time. The earlier reviewed edition remains in history.

### 3. Assess the actual requirements

Under **Requirements**, record the original clause and classify it as mandatory, rated, contractual, informational or unknown. Record its applicability, reviewer, review time, owner, clarification question and next due time.

Add source and supplier evidence separately. Select the exact saved document edition, page/section, relevant extract and reference note. A source reference identifies the requirement; supplier evidence supports the company’s answer.

The assessment choices are **UNREVIEWED**, **MET**, **NOT_MET**, **UNKNOWN** and **NOT_APPLICABLE**. A met assessment requires an explicit review plus source and supplier references. A not-applicable assessment records the applicability basis. Material edits to the clause, classification, applicability or references reset the assessment unless an explicit new review is supplied.

A document’s later edition does not replace the referenced earlier edition. The decision review identifies documents that changed after a requirement assessment, while retaining both the reviewed edition and the current edition where needed.

### 4. Review the context and save the decision

Under **Decision & reports**, choose the notice edition and company profile revision. **Use current notice and profile** explicitly selects their current editions. If reviewing a historical notice edition, select it and acknowledge that choice.

Record **Bid**, **No bid**, **Investigate** or **Park**, with rationale, decision owner, conditions, open questions, reviewer and complete next actions. Each action has a stable identity, task, owner, due time and open/done/cancelled state.

Press **Review selected context**. The page displays all capability checks, mandatory-review issues and changed-document issues. The model returns a digest for the complete context reviewed. Saving the decision supplies that digest inside the same SQLite transaction that rechecks the selected context. If the source, profile, documents or requirement editions changed during the review, the save asks for reassessment.

Every saved decision contains its original source row and metadata, company profile, evidence metadata, requirements, capability assessment, review, actions and context digest. A new decision or substantive decision edit records the reviewed context. A native administrative patch containing only owner and/or next actions preserves the prior frozen context, assessment and review time.

The four choices are available with the recorded evidence and open questions. The fit engine does not turn a match into a bid decision or silently replace the reviewer’s choice.

### 5. Compare and deliver

**Compare saved decision with current records** compares the frozen decision against the latest retained notice, profile, evidence and requirements. It shows complete before/after values and reassessment reasons. It does not overwrite the saved decision.

Download an HTML, JSON or CSV report for any selected decision revision. HTML is a standalone reading copy. JSON retains the full saved envelope. CSV includes typed sections for the decision, actions, source fields, profile, fit checks, requirements, document references and changes. Spreadsheet display cells are escaped while JSON retains original values.

**Download selected workspace package** carries the selected notice history, complete included CSV bodies, original workshares and all referenced bidder records. The bidder graph includes every earlier edition through each selected head, exact evidence bodies and relevant command receipts. A full-workspace package includes all saved profiles and documents, including work that has no decision yet.

Receive through the original **Sources & handoffs** view, native CLI, HTTP client or merchant tools. The receiving transaction validates all included source and record identities before committing. Matching history is reused; new consistent editions append; an incoming older head never replaces a newer local head. Divergent histories or command receipts are retained with the complete incoming bidder package in the saved receiving result for review.

## Data semantics

The implementation reads the actual bilingual CanadaBuys columns retained by the existing source model. Tender status and award status are interpreted in their own source context. Missing data and literal unknown codes remain unknown.

CanadaBuys documents the tender closing field with a fixed UTC−05:00 basis. The original parser and bidder checks preserve the original wall time and offset; they do not substitute a daylight-saving timezone. See the official [CSV support guide](https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/csv-file-support).

Commodity code families remain explicit. A code declared as UNSPSC is not compared as GSIN. Region declarations carry their family and explanatory note; a supplier address or geographic match does not establish a procurement eligibility clause.

The profile’s delivery availability is compared with a retained expected performance start where available. Minimum preparation days use the tender deadline. Contract values remain separate from authored commercial preferences, and an absent original value does not become zero.

Awards and standing offers/supply arrangements remain available through the original notice relationships and full workspace. Their original reference, solicitation, contract and supplier fields retain their source identities. The bidder feature does not add a second source acquisition process.

## Native and HTTP use

All mutations use explicit revisions. Creating a record uses the current workspace revision. Updating a record uses that record’s current revision. A stable command ID identifies a complete save input and its committed result.

The browser maintains the same command ID for an unchanged retry. Native clients can do the same. A repeated committed save returns the original record and current workspace metadata, with alreadyApplied. Reusing the same command ID for different input returns a conflict.

### A saved profile and decision with the Node client

Use the actual running operator origin and retained notice ID. Fill the company statement from the business being reviewed.

~~~js
import { CanadaBuysClient } from './client.mjs';

const client = new CanadaBuysClient(operatorOrigin);
let { workspace } = await client.bidderStatus();

const profileResult = await client.bidderCreate('profile', {
  commandId: profileSaveCommandId,
  label: company.profileName,
  legalName: company.legalName,
  description: company.capabilities,
  keywords: company.searchTerms,
  commodityCodes: company.commodityCodes,
  deliveryRegions: company.deliveryRegions,
  qualificationClaims: company.qualificationClaims,
  capacity: company.capacity,
  commercial: company.commercial
}, workspace.revision);

const notice = await client.notice(noticeId);
const profile = profileResult.record;
const selection = {
  noticeId: notice.id,
  sourceEntryId: notice.currentEntry.id,
  profileId: profile.id,
  profileRevision: profile.revision
};

const reviewed = await client.bidderAssess(selection);
// Present reviewed.context and reviewed.assessment to the reviewer.
({ workspace } = await client.bidderStatus());
const saved = await client.bidderCreate('decision', {
  ...selection,
  contextSha256: reviewed.contextSha256,
  commandId: decisionSaveCommandId,
  choice: reviewer.choice,
  rationale: reviewer.rationale,
  reviewedBy: reviewer.name,
  owner: reviewer.owner,
  unknowns: reviewer.openQuestions,
  conditions: reviewer.conditions,
  nextActions: reviewer.actions
}, workspace.revision);

const report = await client.bidderReport(saved.record.id, {
  revision: saved.record.revision, format: 'html'
});
const comparison = await client.bidderComparison(saved.record.id);
~~~

The API never changes the reviewed context merely because another source, profile or evidence revision has appeared. A changed context returns DECISION_CONTEXT_REVIEW_REQUIRED; read and review the new context, then submit its digest.

### Actual evidence bytes

~~~js
const body = await readFile(originalDocumentPath);
const state = await client.bidderStatus();
const saved = await client.bidderCreate('evidence', {
  commandId: documentSaveCommandId,
  noticeId,
  title: originalDocumentTitle,
  kind: 'SOLICITATION',
  sourceUrl: originalDocumentUrl,
  localOrigin: originalDocumentName,
  bodyBase64: body.toString('base64'),
  version: publisherVersion,
  language: 'en'
}, state.workspace.revision);

const download = await client.bidderEvidence(saved.record.id, {
  revision: saved.record.revision
});
// download.body is a Uint8Array containing the exact saved bytes.
~~~

To update only a nested field, provide only that field. For example, a capacity-state update retains the original availability, lead time and note. Changing a document’s review note retains its other review fields unless a material document change requires a new review.

### CLI

The source command and installed canadabuys command expose the same operations. Use canadabuys help for the complete existing source/workshare/merchant commands.

~~~bash
canadabuys bidder-status --workspace /absolute/procurement
canadabuys bidder-list --workspace /absolute/procurement --kind profile
canadabuys bidder-create --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --kind profile --file /absolute/company-profile.json \
  --expected-revision 4 --command-id company-profile-first-save

canadabuys bidder-create --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --kind evidence --notice-id ORIGINAL_NOTICE_ID \
  --file /absolute/document-description.json \
  --attachment /absolute/original-solicitation.pdf \
  --expected-revision 5 --command-id solicitation-first-save

canadabuys bidder-assess --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --file /absolute/decision-selection.json --out /absolute/review-context.json

canadabuys bidder-create --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --kind decision --file /absolute/reviewed-decision.json \
  --expected-revision 6 --command-id reviewed-decision-first-save

canadabuys bidder-record --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --kind decision --record-id ORIGINAL_DECISION_ID --history
canadabuys bidder-report --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --record-id ORIGINAL_DECISION_ID --revision 1 \
  --format html --out /absolute/decision-r1.html
canadabuys bidder-compare --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --record-id ORIGINAL_DECISION_ID

canadabuys package --workspace /absolute/procurement \
  --scope selected --notice-id ORIGINAL_NOTICE_ID \
  --out /absolute/complete-notice-package.json
canadabuys receive --workspace /absolute/received-procurement \
  --file /absolute/complete-notice-package.json --expected-revision 0
~~~

The shown revision numbers illustrate the sequence; use the actual current revision returned by the workspace. reviewed-decision.json includes the exact contextSha256 from the reviewed assessment, the selected notice/profile and the human-authored decision fields. Native output files use a new destination and are not overwritten.

### HTTP routes

| Operation | Method and route |
| --- | --- |
| Saved counts/current workspace | GET /api/bidder/status |
| Complete record page | GET /api/bidder/records/{kind}?offset=0&limit=100 |
| Saved edition and history | GET /api/bidder/records/{kind}/{id}?revision=1&history=true |
| Create saved record | POST /api/bidder/records/{kind} |
| Append record edition | PATCH /api/bidder/records/{kind}/{id} |
| Profile fit | POST /api/bidder/fit |
| Exact reviewed decision context | POST /api/bidder/assess |
| Current comparison | GET /api/bidder/decisions/{id}/compare |
| Saved decision report | GET /api/bidder/decisions/{id}/report?format=html&revision=1 |
| Original evidence bytes | GET /api/bidder/evidence/{id}/file?revision=1 |

Record lists return page.nextOffset. Continue until null to obtain the full collection. Evidence and requirement lists may be selected by noticeId. Omitting the evidence selection includes company documents and documents from every retained notice.

The existing host/origin checks and request capacity apply. The service listens on the original loopback address; documents are downloaded as attachments.

## Merchant and provider integration

The existing provider adds eight bidder tools: status, list, record, create, update, fit, assess and compare. Each uses the host-declared workspace alias and the same model. The create/update tools accept the full record object and explicit revision. Evidence can consume an inspected, hash-pinned configured input alias; the provider does not accept an arbitrary filesystem path.

merchant_canadabuys_export adds decision-html, decision-json, decision-csv and evidence formats. Select decisionId or evidenceId and optional recordRevision. The existing publication, file listing, exact chunk read and release tools deliver the complete output.

The original SF30 merchant packages the entire selected v2 workspace once and transmits it through its existing immutable dataset. The SF100 adopter reconstructs every selected package part, validates original content, merges consistent bidder histories/evidence/command receipts and passes the result through the same receiving transaction.

Typed exports are included for the native bidder desk, its domain values and report API, alongside the existing workspace and client exports.

## Schema migration and compatibility

Opening an original workspace v1 preserves the original workspace UUID, sources, source observations, reviews, workshares, captures, publications and receiving history. The constructor creates the bidder tables and advances metadata to workspace v2 in one migration transaction. A migration audit entry and one workspace revision record that change. Reopening a v2 workspace does not repeat it.

New packages use package v2 and require their complete bidder payload. The current receiver also accepts a complete original package v1. Older application versions reject workspace/package v2, which prevents an old client from silently exporting a project without the bidder records.

Evidence bodies, record editions, command receipts and receiving are committed through the same original SQLite transaction. Decisions retain acquisition provenance from the reviewed source. During receiving, deterministic row-derived values are checked against the source bytes while original capture labels, URLs, response metadata and capture times remain part of the frozen reviewed context.

## Source and validation

The implementation extends the original 27-file CanadaBuys application at commit 5aeebd4531bb388bf074a45a8f907f9186a7eb14 in woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace. Original source intake and full-feed native runs remain with that application.

The source-backed domain review uses retained complete 67-column tender and 80-column award rows from the original October 12, 2026 captures. A small row projection used by an operating/receiving exercise is identified as a projection; the full-feed capture sizes and hashes remain separate original provenance.

The complete receiving programme exercises migration, saved records, evidence changes, reviewed context, retry continuity, reports and cold receiving through the native application. Its result is recorded only after the actual run. Browser review uses the operator page served by that same application.


## Complete original document intake

Use [Import and review an original document set](EVIDENCE_INTAKE.md) to bring the solicitation, financial workbook and amendments into the existing desk together. The browser preview and Node command save one transaction of ordinary evidence records, retain the unchanged request for recovery, and carry the originals through complete receiving packages.

# CanadaBuys procurement workspace

The **Bidder desk** adds saved company profiles, original evidence documents, clause assessments and versioned Bid / No bid / Investigate / Park decisions to this same workspace. Open it from the procurement navigation. See [the complete bidder desk operating and integration guide](BIDDER_DESK.md) for its browser, CLI, client, merchant and package-receiving workflow.

Operate federal tender, award and standing-offer/supply-arrangement sources in one saved workspace. The browser, CLI, JavaScript client, Applications entry and merchant MCP provider use the same SQLite model. The working product covers source intake, bilingual notice review, exact edition comparison, qualification, supplier research, partner workshare planning, complete handover and merchant delivery.

## Open the application

Use the **CanadaBuys procurement** entry in Applications and select a workspace directory and operator name. Its existing Review/Save/Start/Open/Stop lifecycle owns the local service. In a source checkout:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/procurement --operator "Delivery team"
~~~

The command prints its actual loopback address and workspace identity. Open that address. The [operator guide](operator/README.md) covers source intake, review, workshare economics, exports and receiving. The interface uses a restrained monochrome layout and shows the original source next to saved decisions.

Use the maintained Node runtime with built-in node:sqlite. The source-owned distribution contribution adds the canadabuys command, typed package exports, Applications provider and independent MCP provider; the existing SF30 and merchant components carry the complete files. Native seller dependencies are prepared by the existing distribution runtime profile when using seller service commands.

## Work an opportunity from its original source

1. Import or capture an entire official CSV. The workspace retains every column, every record, original UTF-8 bytes, byte length and SHA256. A separate observation records each import/capture even when the bytes repeat.
2. Search the notice rail and open an original record. Read both languages, closing time, original attachment URLs and complete CSV fields. Exact prior editions remain available for comparison.
3. Save the operator review and source-linked qualification requirements. Each requirement has its source, review state and note. An explicit profile can match keywords, categories, exact GSIN or UNSPSC codes and preparation time.
4. Inspect award candidates linked through the original solicitation numbers, including historical editions. Contract groups show their current edition and all retained originals. Supplier and commodity matches carry explicit evidence.
5. Create a partner workshare. Save scope, deliverables, responsibilities, inputs, acceptance, owner, available date, production/partner hours, delivery days, fee, costs and milestones. Each saved edition retains the original notice context.
6. Export a selected handover or complete workspace. Receive the same package in another workspace. Original source bytes, selected reviews and every workshare edition travel together; existing receiving decisions remain available with any incoming conflicts.

[APM2 operating content](operator/APM2_OPERATING_CONTENT.mjs) applies this complete workflow to the retained Shared Services Canada observability RFI BPM026762/35133. It supplies editable source-linked requirements and an explicit internal delivery proposal. [The original browser journey](operator/OPERATING_JOURNEY.mjs) operates a caller-provided real Page, original server and receiving server.

## CLI and client

Run canadabuys help for complete commands. The installed distribution exposes the same command through starforge canadabuys. Use the current revision returned by status before a workspace mutation:

~~~sh
starforge canadabuys status --workspace /absolute/private/procurement
starforge canadabuys import --workspace /absolute/private/procurement \
  --file /absolute/sources/openTenderNotice.csv --stream open-tenders \
  --retrieved-at 2026-10-12T16:34:03Z --expected-revision 0
starforge canadabuys notice --workspace /absolute/private/procurement \
  --notice-id notice-e7a769311f5a3c763d253568
~~~

Review and workshare update commands use the selected record's own revision. Create/import/capture/receive use the global workspace revision. JSON input files carry complete review, qualification or workshare fields; output files are created with exclusive creation and private permissions.

~~~js
import { CanadaBuysClient } from './client.mjs';
const client = new CanadaBuysClient('http://127.0.0.1:ACTUAL_PORT');
const view = await client.workspace();
const result = await client.capture({
  stream: 'open-tenders',
  expectedRevision: view.revision
});
const notice = await client.notice('notice-e7a769311f5a3c763d253568');
await client.updateReview(notice.id, {
  expectedRevision: notice.review.revision,
  disposition: 'reviewing',
  shortlisted: true,
  owner: 'Delivery team',
  nextAction: 'Complete the source-linked technical response and partner workshare.'
});
~~~

The client supports source/entry/history reads, comparisons, all saved workshare operations, profile matching, capture resumption, reports, packages and receiving. It retains the server error code/status/details. Source captures allow 195 seconds by default; each request accepts timeoutMs and the client accepts a maximum response size. Complete-feed source and JSON envelopes use a 256 MiB default capacity.

## Source semantics

The [official dataset guide](https://donnees-data.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/ba2/ac-cb/soutien-support-eng.html), [tender/award dictionary](https://donnees-data.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/ba2/ac-cb/achatscanada-canadabuys-dd.xml) and [CanadaBuys data page](https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/procurement-and-contracting-data) define the original fields.

- The datasets cover federal procurement. English and French columns belong to the same original record.
- A source closing time without an explicit offset is interpreted at fixed UTC−05:00. Current time is evaluated in live views; immutable entry summaries retain clock-independent raw/UTC values.
- CSV parsing retains multiline quoted descriptions, escaped quotes, BOM, CRLF, empty values and unknown columns. All rows must match the complete header. The original CSV download is byte-preserving.
- The most recent observed complete open feed determines presence. An empty new-tender feed leaves that observation unchanged. A notice absent from the latest open feed retains its last source-reported status separately.
- Tender/award joins use solicitation numbers. All matching historical notice entries are recorded. Reference identifiers remain original values.
- Award amount and cumulative total contract value are separate. Blank award currency uses the official CAD default with the blank original field retained. Contract amounts include taxes. Negative source amounts and alphanumeric amendments remain intact. Repeated cumulative totals are kept in their original contract editions.
- GSIN and UNSPSC are distinct code schemes. Matching uses exact same-scheme codes. Suggested crosswalks require their own source and interpretation.
- Money entered for a workshare uses exact nonnegative integer cents. Delivery days are whole days; production/partner hours can be fractional. The displayed margin is fee minus entered costs, before unentered labor and other costs.

Complete current source metadata and original samples are retained under examples/source/. Source data is subject to the [Open Government Licence – Canada](https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada).

## Original operation and receiving

Each source has a content identity plus separate observations. Repeated imports retain the same source bytes while recording the new retrieval. Reads use a consistent SQLite snapshot; writes acquire the original transaction and check the relevant revision. Indexed notice, solicitation, supplier and commodity lookups support full official feeds.

Each capture has one identity, original URL/stream, revision, lease, response metadata, attempt history and resumption state. Resume the saved captureId after inspecting its result. The same transaction retains its complete source and completion. Retry-After is preserved. The source transport accepts the official HTTPS CSV hosts and validates redirects.

A selected package contains the selected workshare history and necessary original sources, including the latest open-feed source even when selected membership is empty. Its receiving provenance is projected onto that source selection. A full package retains complete workspace history. Receiving verifies source bytes, selected entry identities, source observations, every original workshare edition and the final head. It preserves existing decisions and records incoming conflicts.

## Merchant and agent operation

The independent provider is canadabuys-workspaces, with configuration key canadabuysWorkspaces and connection input canadabuysWorkspaceConnection. The connection schema is starforge.canadabuys.workspace-connection.v1:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "starforge.canadabuys.workspace-connection.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "procurement": {
      "directory": "./procurement",
      "operator": "Delivery team",
      "inputs": {
        "open": {
          "file": "./sources/openTenderNotice.csv",
          "stream": "open-tenders",
          "url": "https://canadabuys.canada.ca/opendata/pub/openTenderNotice-ouvertAvisAppelOffres.csv"
        }
      },
      "deliveries": {
        "partner": "./received-dataset"
      }
    }
  }
}
~~~

Use merchant_canadabuys_workspaces, open and status to select the owned service. Collection pages return nextOffset. Export reports, complete packages, original CSV or exact row JSON; receive listed files through the existing hash-pinned retained-file reader. Close the returned service instance ID.

The merchant commands use the maintained SF30 dataset compiler and native seller. One selected workspace packet includes each complete original source once. Its CSV transport divides that packet into complete 24 KiB Base64 parts with original part/payload hashes. Metadata lists all selected notice IDs. A single-notice packet supports where_notice_id; every packet supports where_package_id. Continue the native page cursor unchanged and retain every transport column.

merchant-prepare freezes the complete selected review/workshare package before asynchronous file work. Public payment terms plus an HTTPS origin configure the native seller; the existing host controls own its instance. The original finalized SF100 delivery is checked for its page chain, manifest, snapshot, output bytes and all packet parts before native receiving. This preserves the selected source and authored work through the maintained commerce protocol.

### Standing offers and supply arrangements

The SOSA importer reads the current 19-column federal schema and retains all original values. The agreement number identifies the instrument. The source field `award-date` is its start date; expiry and file publication remain separate. Legal, operating and standardized supplier names are retained individually. Standardized names group related suppliers for search and never establish a shared legal identity.

The SOSA dictionary calls `commodity` a generic procurement code without naming a classification scheme. Matching code values can produce a candidate with `sourceScheme: unspecified` and `requiresSchemeConfirmation: true`; GSIN and UNSPSC remain separate on tender and award records. Date fields and membership in the published feed never fabricate an explicit instrument status. The original dictionary is included under `examples/source/sosa-dictionary.xml`.

	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at CFB Halifax (and its satellite sites in Nova Scotia) for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029).
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As "Opportunities to bid" arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder's legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:
	
		Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
		Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
		Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
		Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
		Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
		Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada’s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC’s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
		Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada’s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. In this case, the MERX Ad specific to the invitation will clearly identify the inclusion of an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP).
	
	
	Contractors are advised that contracts awarded by DCC include measurable performance standards and requirements as detailed in form DCL81-Performance Evaluation Guidelines which is available at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor that receives an unacceptable or failing score may be removed from this OCSL and receive no further invitations under the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that all contracts tendered and awarded by DCC are subject to DCC’s Procurement Code of Conduct which is available for download at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or a supplier that has been declared ineligible or has been suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and the period of ineligibility or suspension has not expired may be removed from this OCSL and received no further invitations.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that DCC’s Standard Construction Contract Documents - Electronic Bidding (DCL250) will be used for opportunities under the OCSL and can be downloaded from the DCC website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that tenders and contracts under this OCSL may contain organization and personnel security requirements. Typically, the organization security requirement will be Designated Organization Screening (DOS) and reliability status for personnel. However more stringent requirement may apply such as Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of SECRET with approved Document Safeguarding (DSC) with secret clearance for personnel.
	DCC may publish Advance Procurement Notices (APN) identifying potential tenders with anticipated security requirements to provide interested contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship request process for potentially obtaining the required security clearance(s) that are anticipated. The process to apply for a security clearance is provided in the APNs.
	DCC reserves the right to reject any application that does not demonstrate, to the sole satisfaction of DCC, that the contractor or supplier has met the stated requirements. DCC also reserves the right to request clarifications and/or confirmations from any or all firms regarding any aspect of their submission information. A written response to each such communication is required from the firm.
	By submitting a response to this invitation, contractors and suppliers are providing their consent, pursuant to section 30 of the Defence Production Act, for DCC to publicly disclose, after closing, their legal name, address and whether they have been included on the OCSL.
	The OCSL may be used for procurements covered by trade agreements to which Canada is a party.
	You have questions regarding the foregoing, or you wish to be removed from an OCSL, please contact:

Defence Construction Canada
André Champagne

	Construction de Défense Canada (CDC) demande aux entrepreneurs et fournisseurs à présenter une demande d’adhésion à un répertoire ouvert d’entrepreneurs en construction (ROEC) pour des travaux commerciaux, résidentiels, industriels, institutionnels, et de génie civil requis par le ministère de la Défense nationale, à la BFC Halifax (et ses sites satellites à Nouvelle-Écosse) pour trois exercices financiers (du 1er avril 2026 au 31 mars 2029).
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs intéressés peuvent présenter une demande d’adhésion au répertoire à tout moment. Toutefois, CDC demande aux entrepreneurs et fournisseurs intéressés de soumettre leur demande d’adhésion au ROEC dès que possible, de préférence avant le 4 mars 2026. CDC aura besoins de 10 jours ouvrables pour traiter une demande d’adhésion au répertoire.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui désirent adhérer au ROEC doivent soumettre leur demande d’adhésion par le biais de cet affichage MERX et y indiquer leur langue officielle préférée (anglais ou Français).
	IMPORTANT : Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui figuraient au ROEC précédent (du 1er avril 2023 au 31 mars 2026) doivent présenter une nouvelle demande d’adhésion au ROEC pour la période du 1er avril 2026 au 31 mars 2029.
	La langue choisie par le demandeur pour ce répertoire sera la seule langue utilisée pour les documents d’appel d’offres, les documents contractuels et la communication pour toutes les offres futures et pendant l’exécution de tout contrat résultant. La langue choisie s’appliquera pour toute la durée du répertoire.
	Les demandes d’adhésion envoyées par télécopieur, par la poste ou par courriel ne seront pas acceptées. 
	Ce ROEC sera utilisé pour des services de construction (commerciaux, résidentiels, industriels, institutionnels, et de génie civil) d’une valeur estimée à 10 millions de dollars et moins. Au fur et à mesure que des « occasions de soumissionner » se présenteront, CDC invitera tous les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs faisant partie du répertoire à soumissionner pour les travaux.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs seront invités par voie électronique par l’entremise de MERX et pourront, à la discrétion de CDC, être tenus d’assister à une réunion sur place avant la clôture d’un appel d’offres.  Le dépôt des soumissions se fera par voie électronique par l’entremise de MERX.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui présentent une demande d’adhésion au ROEC auront besoin d’un compte MERX actif pour déposer des soumissions électroniques. Veuillez communiquer avec MERX pour savoir comment ouvrir ou réactiver un compte.
	Pour soumissionner dans le cadre d’un appel d’offres, un soumissionnaire doit être inscrit sur le ROEC utilisé pour l’appel d’offres. Si le nom légal du soumissionnaire n’apparaît pas sur le ROEC, CDC pourrait considérer que sa soumission n’est pas conforme. Si vous changez le nom de votre entreprise, il est donc très important que vous en avisiez CDC et que vous envisagiez également d’apporter le changement à votre compte MERX.
	CDC se réserve le droit, à sa seule discrétion, de :
	
		Continuer à utiliser les répertoires déjà en place pour des services similaires ou connexes, tels que les répertoires pour Soumissions à Intervention Rapide (SIR),
		Mettre en place d’autres répertoires pour des catégories spécifiques de services de construction qui peuvent nécessiter des exigences de préqualification différentes, telles que des répertoires pour Soumissions à Intervention Rapide (SIR). Ces autres répertoires ne seront pas annoncés par le biais de ce répertoire. Ces autres répertoires seront annoncés ouvertement sur MERX au cas par cas,
		Vérifiez quels entrepreneurs ont déposé des soumissions en vertu de ce répertoire, vérifiez si ceux qui n’ont pas déposé de soumissions sont toujours intéressés à figurer sur le répertoire et retirer du répertoire les entrepreneurs qui ne sont plus intéressés,
		Exiger des besoins de préqualification supplémentaires pour toute soumission spécifique effectuée par l’intermédiaire du répertoire,
		Choisir d’afficher ouvertement tout appel d’offres sur MERX au lieu d’utiliser le répertoire si CDC estime qu’un appel d’offres ouvert pourrait accroître la concurrence,
		Réserver des appels d’offres aux entreprises autochtones conformément à la Stratégie d’approvisionnement auprès des entreprises autochtones (SAEA). Dans ce cas, tous les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs inscrits au Répertoire ouvert d’entrepreneurs en construction (ROEC) recevront une invitation à soumissionner; toutefois, l’annonce publiée sur MERX indiquera clairement que l’occasion est réservée aux entreprises autochtones en vertu de la SAEA. Pour être admissible, l’entreprise autochtone doit être inscrite au Répertoire des entreprises autochtones (REA) de Services aux Autochtones Canada (SAC). Si vous formez une coentreprise (JV) pour soumissionner sur un contrat réservé aux entreprises autochtones, au moins un membre de la coentreprise doit figurer au ROEC, et l’entreprise autochtone faisant partie de la coentreprise doit également être inscrite au Répertoire des entreprises autochtones de SAC. Le non-respect de ces exigences entraînera le rejet de la soumission pour non-conformité,
		Inclure une exigence de sous-traitance aux entreprises autochtones qui doivent être inscrites dans le Répertoire des entreprises autochtones de Services aux Autochtones Canada (SAC). Dans ce cas, l’annonce MERX spécifique à l’invitation indiquera clairement l’inclusion d’un volet de participation aux Autochtones.
	
	
	Les entrepreneurs sont avisés que les contrats mis en place par CDC comprennent des normes et des exigences de rendement mesurables, comme indiqué dans le formulaire CDL81 - Lignes directrices sur l’évaluation du rendement, disponible à https://www.cdc-dcc.gc.ca/industrie/formulaires. Un entrepreneur qui reçoit une note inacceptable ou une mention d’échec peut être retiré de ce répertoire et ne recevoir aucune autre invitation en vertu de ce répertoire.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs sont avisés que tous les appels d’offres et les contrats mis en place par CDC sont assujettis au Code de conduite en matière d’approvisionnement de CDC, qui peut être téléchargé à l’adresse https://www.cdc-dcc.gc.ca/industrie/formulaires. Un entrepreneur ou un fournisseur qui a été déclaré inadmissible ou qui a été suspendu par Services publics et Approvisionnement Canada en vertu de sa Politique d’inadmissibilité et de suspension et dont la période d’inadmissibilité ou de suspension n’a pas expiré peut être retiré du répertoire et ne recevoir aucune autre invitation.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs sont avisés que les Documents de contrat de construction standards pour soumissions électroniques de CDC (CDL250) seront utilisés pour les opportunités en vertu de ce répertoire et peuvent être téléchargés à partir du site Web de CDC à l’adresse suivante : https://www.cdc-dcc.gc.ca/industrie/formulaires.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs sont avisés que les appels d’offres et les contrats en vertu du présent répertoire peuvent contenir des exigences en matière de sécurité de l’organisation et de sécurité du personnel.  En règle générale, l’exigence de sécurité de l’organisation sera la vérification de l’organisation désignée (VOD) et la cote de fiabilité pour le personnel. Toutefois, des exigences plus strictes peuvent s’appliquer, telles qu’une attestation de sécurité d’installation (ASI), une autorisation de détenir des renseignements (ADR) et une autorisation de sécurité pour son personnel au niveau Secret.
	CDC peut publier des préavis d’approvisionnement (PA) identifiant les appels d’offres potentiels avec des exigences de sécurité prévues afin de donner aux entrepreneurs intéressés l’occasion d’entamer le processus de demande de parrainage pour obtenir éventuellement la ou les cotes de sécurité requises qui sont prévues. Le processus de demande cote de sécurité est fourni dans les PA.
	CDC se réserve le droit de rejeter toute demande de préqualification qui ne démontre pas, à la seule satisfaction de CDC, que l’entrepreneur a satisfait aux exigences énoncées.  CDC se réserve également le droit de demander des éclaircissements ou des confirmations à l’un ou à l’ensemble des entrepreneurs concernant tout aspect des renseignements qu’ils soumettent. Une réponse écrite à chacune de ces communications est requise de la part de l’entrepreneur.
	En répondant à cette invitation, les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs consentent, conformément à l’article 30 de la Loi sur la production de défense, à ce que CDC divulgue publiquement, après la clôture, leur nom légal, leur adresse et s’ils ont été inclus au répertoire.
	Le répertoire peut être utilisée pour les marchés publics visés par des accords commerciaux auxquels le Canada est parti.
	Vous avez des questions concernant ce qui précède ou vous désirez vous retirer d’un répertoire, contactez :

Construction de Défense Canada

<data_dictionary xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://donnees-data.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/dd/spac-pspc-dd.xsd" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" dd_version="1.0">
 <headings>
  <heading id="h1">
   <label>agreement-number</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Agreement number: The standing offer or supply arrangement number. It is a unique identifier for each standing offer or supply arrangement.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Numéro d'accord : le numéro d'une offre à commandes ou d'un arrangement en matière d'approvisionnement. Il s'agit d'un code d'identification unique d'une offre à commandes ou d'un arrangement en matière d'approvisionnement.</description>
  </heading>

  <heading id="h2">
   <label xml:lang="en">agreement-type_en</label>
   <label xml:lang="fr">agreement-type_fr</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Agreement type: The type of agreement, either a supply arrangement or one of the following standing offer types: National Master Standing Offer (NMSO), Departmental Individual Standing Offer (DISO), Regional Individual Standing Offer (RISO), Regional Master Standing Offer</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Type d'accord : il s'agit d'un arrangement en matière d'approvisionnement ou de l'un des types d'offres à commandes suivantes : offre à commandes principale et nationale (OCPN), offre à commandes individuelle et ministérielle (OCIM), offre à commandes individuelle et régionale (OCIR), offre à commandes principale et régionale (OCPR), offre à commandes individuelle et nationale (OCIN).</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h3">
   <label>award-date</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Start date: The start date for the standing offer or supply arrangement.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Date de début : la date de début d'une offre à commandes ou d'un arrangement en matière d'approvisionnement.</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h4">
   <label>commodity</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Commodity: Code used by the federal government to identify generic product descriptions for its procurement activities.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Produit : code utilisé par le gouvernement fédéral pour identifier les descriptions de produits génériques aux fins de ses activités d'achat.</description>
  </heading>

  <heading id="h5">
   <label xml:lang="en">commodity-description_en</label>
   <label xml:lang="fr">commodity-description_fr</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Commodity description: The description of the good or service that corresponds to the commodity code.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Description du produit : la description du bien ou du service correspondant au code du produit.</description>
  </heading>
  
 <heading id="h6">
   <label>date-file-published</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Date file published: The date and time when the file was published.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Date de publication du fichier: La date et l'heure de publication du fichier.</description>
  </heading>
  
  <heading id="h7">
   <label xml:lang="en">delivery-point_en</label>
   <label xml:lang="fr">delivery-point_fr</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Region of delivery: The geographic coverage of the standing offer or supply arrangement, which may be subject to certain delivery terms and conditions specified in the agreement, such as sub-regional delivery points, and Comprehensive Land Claim Agreements (CLCA).</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Région de livraison : la couverture géographique d'une offre à commandes ou d'un arrangement en matière d'approvisionnement qui pourrait être assujettie à certaines modalités de livraison prévues au contrat, comme les points de livraison infrarégionaux, et aux ententes sur les revendications territoriales globales (ERTG).</description>
  </heading>
  
  <heading id="h8">
   <label>delivery-point-code</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Region of delivery code: A geographic code used to identify Canadian provinces and territories as defined in the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 3166-2. Please note that the following three codes are not found in the ISO 3166-2:

FD
Foreign
NA
National - Canada
NC
National Capital</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Code de la région de livraison : un code géographique utilisé pour désigner les provinces et les territoires du Canada, tel que défini dans la norme 3166-2 de l'Organisation internationale de normalisation (ISO). Veuillez noter que les trois codes suivants ne figurent pas dans la norme ISO 3166-2 :

FD
Étranger
NA
National - Canada
NC
Capitale nationale</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h9">
   <label xml:lang="en">end-user-entity_en</label>
   <label xml:lang="fr">end-user-entity_fr</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">End user: The end user identifies the entity (e.g. client department, agency, Crown corporation) on whose behalf the standing offer or supply arrangement has been put in place.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Utilisateur final : l'utilisateur final est l'entité (p. ex., le ministère client, l'organisme, la Société d'État) au nom de laquelle l'offre à commandes ou l'arrangement en matière d'approvisionnement a été établi.</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h10">
   <label>expiry-date</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Expiry date: The end date of a standing offer or supply arrangement.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Date d'expiration : la date de fin d'une offre à commandes ou d'un arrangement en matière d'approvisionnement.</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h11">
   <label xml:lang="en">sosa-description_en</label>
   <label xml:lang="fr">sosa-description_fr</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Description: A brief description of the good or service, for example: "Armoured transportation services".</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Description : une brève description du bien ou du service (par exemple, « services de transport en véhicules blindés »).</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h12">
   <label>supplier-legal-name</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Supplier legal name: Legal registered name of a business entity that is also a supplier to the Government of Canada.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Dénomination sociale du fournisseur : dénomination sociale enregistrée d'une entité commerciale qui est également un fournisseur du gouvernement du Canada.</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h13">
   <label>supplier-operating-name</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Supplier operating name: Name(s) a business entity normally uses when conducting business as a supplier to the Government of Canada.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Nom commercial du fournisseur : le nom qu'une entité commerciale utilise habituellement lorsqu'elle fait des affaires à titre de fournisseur du gouvernement du Canada.</description>
  </heading>
 
  <heading id="h14">
   <label>supplier-standardized-name</label>
   <description xml:lang="en">Supplier standardized name: A supplier name used to simplify search results by grouping together closely related suppliers that conduct business using different operating or legal names. The resulting search records will contain the suppliers' legal and operating names.</description>
   <description xml:lang="fr">Nom normalisé du fournisseur : un nom du fournisseur utilisé pour simplifier les résultats de recherche en regroupant les fournisseurs étroitement liés qui font des affaires sous différents noms commerciaux ou légaux. les dossiers de recherche subséquents contiendront les noms légaux ou commerciaux des fournisseurs.</description>
  </heading>
 
 
    </headings>
</data_dictionary>
