# CanadaBuys customer: original MCP operations and complete receiving

This entry connects a customer or Claude tool workflow to the existing CanadaBuys procurement and bidder workspace. It reads the retained federal source, saves the operator's company profile, evidence, requirement assessments and bid decision, and brings complete published reports or packages back to a local workspace.

The original CanadaBuys application owns the data model, source revisions, decisions and publication files. The customer uses its existing 37 MCP tools. It does not define another source collector, bidder model, payment method or remote upload endpoint.

## Installed entry and source

The existing merchant distribution registers:

- Command: **canadabuys-customer**
- Typed client: **./merchant/canadabuys/client**
- Complete file receiving: **./merchant/canadabuys/download**
- Retained operation requests: **./merchant/canadabuys/operations**

From an original source checkout, use:

    node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/canadabuys-cli.mjs --help

For a source-owned customer release, the maintained builder has the `canadabuys-customer` selection. From the repository root, build the selected immutable commit:

    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
      --repo . --ref YOUR_COMMIT --selection canadabuys-customer \
      --out canadabuys-customer-release

Use the archive path and SHA-256 returned by that build with the original runtime installer:

    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs prepare \
      --dir canadabuys-customer-runtime --archive ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE.tgz \
      --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 --operator
    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs install \
      --dir canadabuys-customer-runtime --offline
    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs inspect \
      --dir canadabuys-customer-runtime --load --source

This workflow selects no external runtime feature: the native workspace uses Node's SQLite support, and the retained writer uses Linux flock. The original installer still records and verifies its dependency lock. Its `--offline` option uses the selected local npm installation and cache. The source archive declares `starforge`, `canadabuys` and `canadabuys-customer` binaries; a normal npm installation exposes those names. With the maintained private runtime layout, dispatch the same installed customer through:

    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs run \
      --dir canadabuys-customer-runtime -- canadabuys-customer --help

The commands below use `canadabuys-customer` as that installed entry. The same runtime dispatch accepts `canadabuys serve --workspace DIRECTORY --operator customer` when opening a received native workspace.

The customer's HTTP transport uses the maintained merchant MCP initialization and tool-call implementation. The original authenticated endpoint must already exist. Its operator selects workspace, input and delivery aliases in the existing merchant configuration. This client does not create that configuration or interpret an arbitrary remote path as an input.

Use Node 24 or later for the whole workflow, including the original SQLite workspace receiving. Local operation and download directories use the repository's existing Linux flock lease, supplied by util-linux. The client itself has no new third-party dependency.

Source contracts:

- Original provider: [canadabuys-workspace.mjs](./canadabuys-workspace.mjs).
- Original 37-tool catalogue: [catalog/canadabuys-workspace.mjs](./catalog/canadabuys-workspace.mjs).
- Original native workspace and package validation: [workspace.mjs](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/workspace.mjs).
- Original bidder persistence and command deduplication: [bidder-desk-workspace.mjs](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/bidder-desk-workspace.mjs).
- Original bidder operator guide: [BIDDER_DESK.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/BIDDER_DESK.md).
- Existing complete file writer: [retained-download.mjs](./retained-download.mjs).
- Existing MCP host/Claude registration: [STDIO.md](./STDIO.md) and [client-config.mjs](./client-config.mjs).

The full customer receiving programme accompanies this entry. Its result must be read as actual execution evidence; this guide does not substitute authored source for a run.

## Connect the original customer

Create a private working directory and connection template:

    umask 077
    mkdir canadabuys-customer-work
    canadabuys-customer connection-template --out canadabuys-customer-work/connection.json

Edit the template to select the actual endpoint, existing host alias and credential environment variable:

    {
      "schema": "stellar-forge.canadabuys-customer-connection.v1",
      "url": "https://your-existing-merchant.example/mcp",
      "tokenEnv": "MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN",
      "workspace": "procurement",
      "workspaceId": null,
      "maximumResponseBytes": 4194304
    }

This URL and alias are illustrative; use the values supplied by the original merchant operator. Populate the selected environment variable through the existing credential mechanism. The connection file contains the environment variable name, never its token value.

Bind that alias to the observed native workspace:

    canadabuys-customer bind \
      --connection canadabuys-customer-work/connection.json \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/bound-connection.json

The returned observation contains the native workspace UUID, revision and original operator browser URL. The saved bound connection retains the observed UUID. Later operations compare that UUID before dispatch; an alias reconfigured to a different workspace is rejected. bind opens the existing original workspace service. Disconnecting the customer leaves that application available.

Keep JSON files private (0600) and directories private (0700). The reader rejects symlinks, replacement during a read and oversized inputs. --out creates the complete result exclusively. Choose a different output filename for a later observation; original result files are not overwritten.

## Read the complete original source

List the exact available input schemas without opening a workspace:

    canadabuys-customer tools --out canadabuys-customer-work/tools.json

Read the current workspace and complete notice collection:

    canadabuys-customer read \
      --connection canadabuys-customer-work/bound-connection.json \
      --tool status --all \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/notices.json

For a different collection, save a request such as:

    {"collection":"sources","limit":100}

Then pass that private JSON through --args. The CLI accepts the short tool name or the original merchant_canadabuys_ name. read permits only original read-only tools. --all follows every actual page.nextOffset and accepts the completed collection only if the native workspace UUID and revision remain unchanged across the read. If the workspace advances, retain those observations and make a new complete read.

Read one notice with noticeId. It includes original editions, current retained row, review, award and arrangement candidates and workshares. Read the exact original source edition with entryId. The full before/after comparison uses beforeId, afterId and includeValues:true; comparisons can also be paged completely.

Original source/body results may exceed the selected MCP response bound. For a large original CSV or package, retain a publication through the original export tool and use the bounded chunk download below. The client never replaces an entire source with a sample.

## Review and save one original request

Read-only observations can be called directly. Changes are prepared as an immutable local request before they are entered.

For example, a company profile request uses the existing bidder_create tool:

    {
      "kind": "profile",
      "expectedRevision": 12,
      "commandId": "company-profile-review-20261013",
      "record": {
        "label": "Reviewed supplier profile",
        "legalName": "Replace with the actual legal entity",
        "description": "Replace with the reviewed capabilities",
        "keywords": [],
        "commodityCodes": [],
        "qualificationClaims": [],
        "evidenceIds": [],
        "notes": "Record the source and reviewer for the declarations."
      }
    }

The revision and business facts above are examples, not current workspace data. Use the actual global revision returned by status and the operator's declarations. Save this JSON, then prepare:

    canadabuys-customer plan \
      --connection canadabuys-customer-work/bound-connection.json \
      --directory canadabuys-customer-work/profile-operation \
      --operation-id company-profile-review-20261013 \
      --tool bidder_create \
      --args canadabuys-customer-work/profile-request.json \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/profile-plan.json

plan is offline. It records the original endpoint identity, alias, native UUID, exact tool and arguments, source-backed replay policy and SHA256 of the complete request bytes. Inspect request.json or the plan output, then enter that request:

    canadabuys-customer run \
      --directory canadabuys-customer-work/profile-operation \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/profile-response.json

run does not invent a newer revision or change fields after a conflict. A changed request needs its own reviewed operation directory. The original bidder commandId provides transactional deduplication for the same create/update input; reusing that ID with different input is a conflict.

For bidder updates, expectedRevision is the selected record's current revision, not the global workspace revision. The wrapper retains the exact original arguments. A repeated native command may return the original saved record with the current workspace metadata and alreadyApplied:true; that is the maintained API's response and is preserved.

## Complete bidder work

The client exposes the whole existing workflow:

| Stage | Original tools | Retained result |
|---|---|---|
| Company capabilities | bidder_status, bidder_list, bidder_record, bidder_create, bidder_update | Original profiles and every saved edition |
| Original evidence | inputs, bidder_create, bidder_update, export with format evidence | Complete configured input bytes, SHA256 and explicit review state |
| Requirement review | bidder_create or bidder_update with kind requirement | Exact source/supplier evidence editions, page/section, assessment and reviewer |
| Fit and current context | bidder_fit, bidder_assess | Original field observations, gaps, unknowns and contextSha256 |
| Reviewed decision | bidder_create or bidder_update with kind decision | Operator choice and rationale bound to exact context |
| Changed context | bidder_compare | Original and current editions with material change evidence |
| Partner work | workshare_create, workshare_update, workshare | Scope, integer-cent costs, milestones and original history |
| Reports and portable copy | export, files, file_read, file_release | Exact complete publication bytes and native workspace package |

A configured evidence input is selected by its host alias and the SHA256 observed through inputs. The provider reads the original file and checks that hash before the native evidence transaction. The customer cannot substitute a local client path for an input alias.

For evidence intake, include kind:evidence, input, expectedSha256 and the original record metadata. The source body, byte count and SHA256 are retained by the provider. Evidence access/review status remains explicit; an unavailable or unreviewed document is not marked reviewed by the client.

For a decision, first read bidder_assess with the exact noticeId, sourceEntryId, profileId and profileRevision. Retain its returned contextSha256. The decision request includes that SHA, the same original selection, the operator's choice and rationale. The native transaction checks the current context again. A new source or evidence edition requires the operator to examine the change; the client does not silently replace the selected context.

Fit output supports review. The existing model distinguishes matches, gaps, unknowns, source timing and mandatory review. It does not make a human bid decision or convert an unknown qualification into eligibility. See the original bidder guide for complete profile, evidence, requirement and decision fields; the customer TypeScript declarations reuse those native types directly.

## Request interruption and recovery

Each local operation retains:

    request.json
    state.json
    attempts/000001/entered.json
    attempts/000001/result.json or error.json
    complete.json
    reconciliations/<evidence-sha256>.json when explicitly adopted

The original Linux lease prevents two writers from entering the same operation directory concurrently. Process exit releases that kernel-owned lease. Saved request and attempt/result files remain immutable.

run publishes entered.json before the original call. It saves the complete result before publishing complete.json. If the response was saved and the parent stopped before completion publication, the same run command recovers that original response without another remote call. Once complete.json exists, run reopens it offline and does not look up credentials.

show is a lock-free saved-progress read. It never opens the provider or retrieves credentials. It may observe the last saved state while another writer is active:

    canadabuys-customer show --directory canadabuys-customer-work/profile-operation

An entered request with no saved response is handled by its actual original contract:

| Request | Reopen behavior |
|---|---|
| Original read-only tool | Repeat the same read; retain its new observation |
| Original open | Reopen the same saved workspace alias and UUID |
| Bidder create/update with commandId | Re-enter the exact original input; native command history resolves a committed result |
| Capture with retained captureId | Continue that original capture and its retained source state |
| Another entered mutation | Preserve RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED; do not repeat it automatically |
| Explicit provider error applied:false | Preserve the error; the same original request may be tried again |

A timeout or transport failure is not proof that a mutation failed. The customer retains that uncertainty. It has no generic force or retry-with-new-ID option.

### Recover an original exported file

The native export creates a new immutable publication. It does not accept an idempotency key. If its reply was lost, read the current publications collection and inspect the actual candidate with files before selecting it.

Create an evidence template for that same original export:

    canadabuys-customer publication-selection \
      --directory canadabuys-customer-work/package-operation \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/package-selection.json

Fill only the observed publicationId and operator note. Preserve operationId and requestSha256, then:

    canadabuys-customer adopt-publication \
      --directory canadabuys-customer-work/package-operation \
      --evidence canadabuys-customer-work/package-selection.json

Adoption reads files for that exact UUID and verifies the original native workspace, format, sourceRevision, selected arguments and file bytes/hash. It records ADOPTED_ORIGINAL_PUBLICATION, the complete evidence note and observed response. It does not call export.

A matching publication is compatible with the entered export; matching fields alone cannot prove uniqueness if another operator made an identical concurrent export. Selecting the original observed UUID is an explicit operator reconciliation. A contradictory publication is rejected.

## Download every original file

A successful export response returns its original publicationId. Inspect the complete publication:

    canadabuys-customer inspect-publication \
      --connection canadabuys-customer-work/bound-connection.json \
      --publication-id ORIGINAL_PUBLICATION_UUID \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/publication-inspection.json

Then retain every original file:

    canadabuys-customer download \
      --connection canadabuys-customer-work/bound-connection.json \
      --publication-id ORIGINAL_PUBLICATION_UUID \
      --directory canadabuys-customer-work/package-download \
      --manifest-sha256 ORIGINAL_INSPECTED_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/package-download-receipt.json

Use the UUID and SHA returned by the actual inspection. The customer-generated canadabuys-publication.json contains the original workspace UUID, full original files response and an exact descriptor for every selected file. That manifest is an explicit client receiving envelope; it is not represented as a server-generated archive.

The transfer uses only the existing files, file_read and file_release tools. The local adapter maps those real operations into the repository's existing retained-file writer. Its internal dispatch labels are not additional MCP endpoints.

The writer preserves:

- Full original relative file names, including native merchant payload directories.
- Original MIME types, byte counts and SHA256.
- The provider's original readId and exact nextOffset.
- Complete native-file bytes, bounded Base64 chunks and final full-file hashing.
- Durable verified partial prefixes and atomic completed file publication.
- Exact original manifest and download checkpoint when resumed.

The native reader reports the basename in its file descriptor. The client checks that original basename before mapping the descriptor to the full relative path already supplied by files. The complete path and original descriptor remain in the client manifest.

If a saved read lease has expired, the existing writer reopens the same original file at the retained offset and verifies the full identity; it does not create another publication. Disconnect closes this client's retained readers. The provider's file_release now returns its structured acknowledgment only after the original release completes, including the absent/already-released case.

Current source bounds are 100,000 original files, 1 GiB per file, 8 GiB total, a 64 MiB complete manifest and a 128 MiB checkpoint. Chunk size is 1–196,608 bytes. These are explicit transfer bounds; exceeding one returns an error without truncating the source. The native MCP service's own input/reply limits still apply.

## Verify and open a complete customer workspace offline

Verify the final files without a connection file or token:

    canadabuys-customer verify \
      --directory canadabuys-customer-work/package-download \
      --publication-id ORIGINAL_PUBLICATION_UUID \
      --manifest-sha256 ORIGINAL_INSPECTED_MANIFEST_SHA256

Verification takes the original local directory lease and checks the completed manifest, checkpoint and every file. It uses no endpoint and sends no network request.

A publication exported with format:package contains the native complete CanadaBuys package. Receive it through the unchanged SQLite model:

    canadabuys-customer receive \
      --directory canadabuys-customer-work/package-download \
      --publication-id ORIGINAL_PUBLICATION_UUID \
      --workspace-directory canadabuys-customer-work/received-workspace \
      --expected-revision 0 \
      --operator customer \
      --out canadabuys-customer-work/receiving.json

Use revision0 only for a new empty workspace; otherwise supply the actual current local revision. The original receiver verifies the full package, original source bodies, saved bidder editions and evidence bytes. It keeps local review/record conflicts and the original receiving history. Reopening the same package preserves later local decisions through the original already-received behavior.

The returned customer receiving receipt binds the original publication UUID, source workspace UUID, manifest SHA256 and exact package file identity to the native receiving result and current local workspace. The source package itself remains byte-identical.

Open the complete received workspace with the installed native application:

    canadabuys serve --workspace canadabuys-customer-work/received-workspace --operator customer

Follow the loopback URL printed by that command, open **Bidder desk**, then **Decision & reports**. The page opens the same received source editions, evidence, requirements and saved decisions. Later local edits remain in that workspace when the original package is received again.

The full application and current customer modules are retained together in the installed distribution and receiving bundle.

## Programmatic use

The same lifecycle is available from the installed typed client:

    import { openCanadaBuysMerchantClient } from '<installed-package>/merchant/canadabuys/client';

    const client = await openCanadaBuysMerchantClient({
      url: originalEndpoint,
      tokenEnv: 'MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN',
      workspace: originalAlias,
      workspaceId: originalNativeUuid
    });
    try {
      await client.open();
      const current = await client.status();
      const records = await client.collect('bidder_list', { kind: 'profile', limit: 100 });
      const publication = await client.inspectPublication(originalPublicationId);
      const downloaded = await client.downloadPublication(originalPublicationId, privateOutputDirectory, {
        expectedManifestSha256: publication.manifestSha256
      });
      // Retain current, records and downloaded through the customer's original workflow.
    } finally {
      await client.disconnect();
    }

<installed-package> denotes the actual merchant distribution selected by the operator. The source checkout imports ./canadabuys-client.mjs directly. The interface does not choose or install a different package.

For a mutation that must survive process loss, use prepareCanadaBuysOperation followed by executeCanadaBuysOperation instead of wrapping a direct call in a generic retry loop. Its saved request is the concrete object to review. An application can read showCanadaBuysOperation during execution and preserve its final complete response beside the downloaded package.

## Completion evidence

A complete customer receiving result should identify:

1. The original native workspace and the full source/notice collection used.
2. Saved original profile, evidence, requirement and decision IDs/revisions.
3. The actual commandId and result used to recover a lost bidder mutation response.
4. The entered export and explicitly adopted original publication when its response was lost.
5. Every downloaded original file identity and the complete client manifest SHA.
6. The original file lease release result and same-file resume after interruption.
7. The full native package and offline receiving result, including a later local edit preserved on repeated receiving.
8. Final service/client drain and all complete source and received artifacts.

Continue operating from the received workspace and its printed application URL. Review the original source edition and evidence in **Decision & reports**, save any next local decision, and retain that workspace with the complete download and receiving receipts.

# Import and review an original document set

The Bidder Desk accepts the original solicitation, financial workbook, amendments and supplier documents together. The browser and Node command use the same saved workspace and evidence engine.

## Operator workflow

1. Open **Bidder desk → Documents & evidence → Import a document set** with the relevant retained notice selected.
2. Choose the original files and, if useful, the publisher's common event URL. **Preview files** reads the exact bytes and shows one editable row per file.
3. Review each title, document type, publisher edition, source URL and issued date. Select an earlier saved document only when the new file actually supersedes it. The filename is initially the title; the type starts as **OTHER** until chosen.
4. **Prepare intake** retains the complete request in this browser. **Download prepared intake** saves the same request, including every original file, for recovery.
5. **Save prepared documents** imports the whole set in one SQLite transaction. Open the saved originals to record the document review, extract the actual requirements and update the decision.

All newly imported documents start **UNREVIEWED**. Capturing bytes does not establish that the document was read or that a contractor satisfies its requirements. A source-list notice, an advance procurement notice and a released tender retain their own procurement stages.

Each file becomes an ordinary native evidence record with its own UUID, SHA-256, byte length, source origin, capture time and saved edition. The existing evidence download, requirement references, decision comparison, HTML/CSV/JSON reports and complete workspace receiving packages continue to use those same records.

## Recovery and concurrent edits

Preparing fixes the original notice, files, metadata and intake identity. Retrying an unchanged prepared request returns its original saved editions without appending another intake.

A changed workspace revision may require **Refresh save revision**, followed by **Save prepared documents**. This refreshes only the transaction's workspace guard; the original input identity and per-document commands stay unchanged. A completed original request still reopens its original records. A different file or metadata value under the same intake identity is rejected.

Use **Restore prepared intake** to load the downloaded JSON into the same workspace. It is bound to the original workspace ID. Receiving a normal complete workspace package on another workstation preserves its native evidence and commands; the intake JSON itself is a recovery request for its original workspace.

The browser retains one current prepared intake per workspace. **Start a new intake** releases that browser copy after confirmation. Keep its downloaded copy if a save still needs recovery. Existing saved documents are unchanged by this action.

The whole set commits together. Invalid bytes, lengths, metadata or an invalid earlier-document reference reject the set; an interrupted or failed SQLite transaction rolls back its evidence records, bodies and native commands.

## Native command

Node 24 with the existing original workspace is sufficient:

~~~sh
node evidence-intake.mjs prepare /path/to/workspace documents.json prepared-intake.json
node evidence-intake.mjs apply /path/to/workspace prepared-intake.json
~~~

The prepare command writes a new file with exclusive creation. It reads original local files and retains their exact bytes. The apply command calls workspace.bidderDesk.intakeEvidence directly.

For an explicitly refreshed transaction guard:

~~~sh
node evidence-intake.mjs refresh-revision /path/to/workspace prepared-intake.json refreshed-intake.json
node evidence-intake.mjs apply /path/to/workspace refreshed-intake.json
~~~

A manifest identifies an existing notice by noticeId or exact solicitationNumber. File paths are relative to the manifest, or absolute. Every document can supply the existing evidence metadata fields. Supplied hashes or byte lengths are checked against the actual file before preparation.

~~~json
{
  "solicitationNumber": "EV9397",
  "sourceUrl": "https://contracts.fin.gov.nt.ca/",
  "documents": [
    {
      "path": "EV9397_-_Procurement_Advisory_Services.pdf",
      "kind": "SOLICITATION",
      "version": "Record the actual publisher edition"
    },
    {
      "path": "EV9397_-_Appendix_B_-_Financial_Submission_Form.xlsx",
      "kind": "ANNEX",
      "version": "Record the actual publisher edition"
    },
    {
      "path": "EV9397-Addendum_No._1.pdf",
      "kind": "AMENDMENT",
      "version": "Addendum No. 1"
    },
    {
      "path": "EV9397-Addendum_No._2.pdf",
      "kind": "AMENDMENT",
      "version": "Addendum No. 2"
    }
  ]
}
~~~

This example names the publicly indexed document set. Download the current issuer originals and any later amendments before preparing it, then replace the publisher-edition labels with the actual editions. The command requires the actual files and retained notice. Its default capture time is when the original local bytes are copied into the intake. Supply capturedAt explicitly when retaining an earlier documented capture time.

The browser and command accept up to 100 files, 64 MiB per file and 128 MiB combined. Existing server request and evidence limits continue to apply.

## Native and HTTP interfaces

- workspace.bidderDesk.intakeEvidence(input)
- client.bidderIntakeEvidence(input)
- POST /api/bidder/evidence-intake

Required input fields are workspaceId, noticeId, expectedRevision, a stable commandId, and documents. Each document has the existing evidence metadata plus complete canonical bodyBase64 and an explicit capturedAt timestamp. Optional sha256 and bytes must match its body. Intake metadata cannot assign record IDs or revisions. Completed reviews are recorded through the existing individual-document workflow.

Optional applyRevision supplies a fresh workspace revision for an explicit retry. It is the only apply field excluded from the original intake digest. The response retains commandId, intakeSha256, noticeId, the original native evidence records, current workspace metadata and alreadyApplied.

The original bidder_commands table keeps one ordinary evidence-create result for each document. Complete package exports and receiving retain these commands and evidence editions without adding another evidence store or package format.

# CanadaBuys: original document intake through the installed customer

The installed customer prepares an RFP, workbook and amendment set from the customer's original files, inspects that complete request through the existing Merchant connection, and saves every document together in the native CanadaBuys workspace. The saved documents remain native evidence records and enter the existing review, requirement, decision, report, export and cold-receiving workflow.

The original engine is CanadaBuysWorkspace.bidderDesk.intakeEvidence. Its SQLite transaction and command history provide the save and replay semantics. The customer and Merchant layers retain the same native request.

## Existing installation and connection

Use the installed **canadabuys-customer** command from the existing Starforge distribution. The Merchant host must already expose the CanadaBuys workspace under its configured alias. Obtain a bound connection through the existing connection-template and bind commands described in [CANADABUYS_CUSTOMER.md](CANADABUYS_CUSTOMER.md). That file retains the actual native workspace UUID, endpoint and credential environment-variable name.

An intake uses the existing host **inputs** configuration. The customer cannot pass an arbitrary host filesystem path over MCP. If customer and Merchant run on different machines, the host operator receives the complete prepared JSON through their existing authorized file-transfer route, verifies its exact bytes and SHA256, and declares that file under an input alias. This guide does not establish a new transfer destination, grant file access or modify a running Merchant's configuration automatically.

Use a private working directory and keep the connection, manifest, prepared request and operation history there. Document requests contain every original file as Base64.

## 1. Select the original notice and files

Read the existing notices:

~~~sh
canadabuys-customer read --connection bound-connection.json \
  --tool status --all --out original-notices.json
canadabuys-customer intake-template --out documents.json
~~~

Edit documents.json to identify the actual saved notice and your complete source files:

~~~json
{
  "noticeId": "REPLACE_WITH_ORIGINAL_NOTICE_ID",
  "commandId": "customer-rfp-original-001",
  "capturedAt": "REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_CAPTURE_TIMESTAMP",
  "sourceUrl": "REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_DOCUMENT_SOURCE_URL",
  "documents": [
    {
      "path": "./rfp.pdf",
      "title": "Original request for proposals",
      "kind": "OTHER",
      "language": "en",
      "pageOrSection": "",
      "notes": "Original source file."
    },
    {
      "path": "./pricing.xlsx",
      "title": "Original pricing workbook",
      "kind": "OTHER",
      "language": "en"
    },
    {
      "path": "./amendment-1.pdf",
      "title": "Original amendment 1",
      "kind": "OTHER",
      "language": "en",
      "version": "1"
    }
  ]
}
~~~

Use the actual capture time, for example an observed ISO 8601 timestamp. Each document can override capturedAt and source metadata. Paths are relative to the manifest. Optional bytes and sha256 fields must agree with the complete original file.

Use a stable command ID for this original batch. It identifies the same documents and intended save; retain it across interruption recovery. Use a new command for a genuinely different batch.

Preparation permits 1–100 regular documents, at most 64 MiB each and 128 MiB combined. Complete prepared JSON is bounded at 192 MiB to accommodate Base64 and metadata. Preparation reads each file on one open handle in bounded chunks and verifies its complete digest, byte length and unchanged inode metadata. It refuses symlink final components.

## 2. Prepare the complete native request

~~~sh
canadabuys-customer prepare-intake \
  --connection bound-connection.json \
  --manifest documents.json \
  --request-out native-intake.json \
  --out intake-preparation.json
~~~

The command reads the actual workspace revision and selected notice through the authenticated MCP connection, reads every original document, and checks that the workspace did not advance during preparation. It publishes native-intake.json through an atomic, create-only file operation. A different existing file is preserved and rejected.

The prepared file contains the native workspaceId, noticeId, expectedRevision, commandId and complete documents. It does not save evidence yet. Its result identifies the complete request file and every document hash. Capture timestamps come from the manifest.

The original local native preparation remains supported:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/evidence-intake.mjs \
  prepare /path/to/original-workspace documents.json native-intake.json
~~~

Both preparations produce the same native intake shape. A request created by the original CLI can be inspected and saved through the installed Merchant.

## 3. Bind the prepared file on the existing Merchant host

The host operator adds the prepared file to the existing workspace's inputs, preserving all other configuration:

~~~json
{
  "inputs": {
    "original-rfp-intake": {
      "file": "./private/native-intake.json",
      "label": "Original RFP, pricing workbook and amendment"
    }
  }
}
~~~

This is a fragment of the existing connection, not a replacement configuration. Use its existing relative-path rules and normal service lifecycle. Do not overwrite another input or the current service's ownership.

Create a private inspect-intake.json:

~~~json
{
  "input": "original-rfp-intake",
  "expectedSha256": "REPLACE_WITH_PREPARATION_REQUEST_FILE_SHA256"
}
~~~

~~~sh
canadabuys-customer read --connection bound-connection.json \
  --tool bidder_intake_inspect --args inspect-intake.json \
  --out original-intake-inspection.json
~~~

Inspection returns the exact file identity, native workspace, original command, notice, revisions, per-document identities and source metadata. It does not return document bodies or mutate the workspace. Native intake performs authoritative metadata and transaction validation when saving.

Inspection rejects changed files, another workspace, invalid Base64, contradictory document identities and exceeded size limits. Missing host inputs remain explicit configuration errors.

## 4. Retain and run one original intake operation

~~~sh
canadabuys-customer intake-plan \
  --connection bound-connection.json \
  --input original-rfp-intake \
  --expected-sha256 REPLACE_WITH_PREPARATION_REQUEST_FILE_SHA256 \
  --directory original-intake-operation \
  --operation-id customer-rfp-original-001 \
  --out original-intake-plan.json

canadabuys-customer show --directory original-intake-operation
canadabuys-customer run --directory original-intake-operation \
  --out original-intake-save.json
~~~

Intake-plan performs a read-only inspection, then calls the existing durable operation planner. Its immutable request retains the input alias, exact file SHA256, native UUID, notice, command and original save revisions.

Run calls merchant_canadabuys_bidder_intake. The provider rereads and verifies that exact input, then passes its complete native request to intakeEvidence. It does not loop over separate per-document create operations. Every record commits together in the original transaction or none of that batch commits.

The result retains the native intake schema, command ID, intake digest, notice ID, original evidence editions and current workspace metadata. The alreadyApplied field identifies native replay.

After a lost response, run the same saved operation again. Its replay policy binds both the original command and input SHA256. Native command history returns the original editions even if later reviews created newer editions. The customer retains the returned result before publishing completion. Reopening a completed operation uses that saved result without another call.

Do not overwrite the configured input with different bytes to force a retry. Changed input is rejected before the native mutation.

## 5. Resolve an actual revision conflict

Another valid workspace change can occur before save. Preserve the original request and failed operation, then explicitly select the current save revision:

~~~sh
canadabuys-customer refresh-intake \
  --connection bound-connection.json \
  --request native-intake.json \
  --request-out native-intake-refreshed.json \
  --out intake-save-revision.json
~~~

This retains every original field, including expectedRevision, command and document bytes, and changes only applyRevision to the observed current revision. It creates a separate file. The result binds that file to the original request's path, length and SHA256.

Declare the refreshed file under a separate host input alias, inspect it, and plan a new customer operation directory around that exact file. Keep the same native command ID. Native intake excludes applyRevision from its original intake identity, so an already committed batch returns its original records. A different document or authored metadata under the same command is rejected.

The new operation directory records an explicitly changed file selection. Retain the previous immutable request and attempt history.

## Review, export and cold receiving

Read returned evidence IDs with bidder_record and complete the existing human review workflow. Incoming documents begin unreviewed. Intake cannot assert that someone reviewed a source. Use saved evidence editions for requirement references and retain amendments as explicit source history.

The existing export tool exports a selected evidence edition's exact bytes with format evidence, or the complete native package with format package. Keep its original publication UUID, download every listed file, verify offline and receive through the installed commands in the customer guide. The native package retains evidence bytes, editions and command history, allowing cold receiving to reconcile the same intake with its original IDs.

After receiving, open the actual installed workspace:

~~~sh
canadabuys serve --workspace /path/to/received-workspace --operator customer
~~~

Open its printed loopback URL, then **Bidder desk → Decision & reports**. Receiving does not imply purchase, payment or completed source review.

## JavaScript and MCP surface

CanadaBuysMerchantClient exposes inspectEvidenceIntake(args) and intakeEvidence(args). The existing installed operations module exports:

- prepareCanadaBuysEvidenceIntake({client, manifestPath, outputPath, signal})
- refreshCanadaBuysEvidenceIntake({client, requestPath, outputPath, signal})
- prepareCanadaBuysIntakeOperation({client, connection, directory, operationId, input, expectedSha256, signal})

The catalogue adds merchant_canadabuys_bidder_intake_inspect as read-only and merchant_canadabuys_bidder_intake as native-command idempotent. Existing tool names, operations, source configuration, service lifetime and download contracts remain compatible.

# CanadaBuys desk — operator guide

Use **Bidder desk** in the navigation for saved company capabilities, original evidence documents, clause assessments, reviewed decisions and revision-specific reports. Its [complete operating guide](../BIDDER_DESK.md) describes how this page shares the original source and workspace below.

The desk joins an original CanadaBuys source edition to a usable procurement review and partner workshare. It opens the full bilingual notice, retains its original CSV fields and attachments, records the requirements and delivery fit, and carries the scope, production capacity, partner responsibilities and milestone cash into a saved handover.

The browser uses the same local application and native workspace as the command-line client and provider. Its procurement page and bidder desk are complete, dependency-free HTML files. The application server serves it at the workspace address; open the URL printed by that server. Source acquisition, storage, revisions, reports and package receiving remain with the original CanadaBuys domain.

## 1. Bring in the original source

Open **Import source**, select the actual stream, and choose the original CSV. Supported streams are:

| Stream | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Open tenders | A complete edition of currently open federal notices |
| New tenders | The published new-notice stream, including a valid header-only edition |
| Complete tender history | Original historical tender rows |
| Contract awards | Award and amendment source rows |
| Standing offers and supply arrangements | Original instrument and supplier information |

Keep the original publication URL, retrieval time and supplied SHA-256 when available. The file reader preserves UTF-8, the original byte-order mark, CRLF and quoted multiline content. The server parses the CSV and retains its original complete text. The text area can also accept an intentionally prepared CSV edition.

Under **Sources & handoffs**, choose a stream and use **Fetch and retain official stream** to have the existing server acquire the original publication directly. Each capture has its own original operation record and HTTP/source metadata. A continuation button appears only when the returned original capture explicitly supports continuation.

A zero-row new-tender file is a legitimate source edition. Its presence does not imply that the last complete open-tender edition is empty. The **In latest open feed** field belongs to the original complete-open membership snapshot. The last source status stays separate, so a retained notice can have original status Open while absent from a newer complete-open feed.

## 2. Find and read a notice

The notice list searches identifiers, titles, buyers, both descriptions, commodity codes, review ownership and working notes. Every search word must appear in that searchable text. The filters select the original notice type, review disposition, closing window, delivery region, shortlist and latest-open membership.

The list shows 40 notices per page. Select individual notices or **Select page** to build a report selection. Changing a filter preserves the selected identifiers. The selected report option requires at least one selected notice.

Open a notice to choose its retained source row and read the full description in English, French or both languages. HTML character references are decoded for the readable description, and text remains inert. **Original source** retains the exact original field values, including their original markup and punctuation.

The original title and notice-type field stay distinct. An advance procurement notice can have a blank source type. A source type can say Request for Proposal while its description describes an RFQ. Read the complete source and original attachments for the actual buying phase and requirements.

The source contract includes real examples of these distinctions:

- APM2 describes an information-gathering phase for enterprise infrastructure, application and datacentre observability.
- Managed Backup and Recovery Software describes an Invitation to Qualify whose successful respondents can enter later procurement phases.
- HPE renewal describes an RFQ and its responsive, lowest-evaluated-subtotal selection alongside the original source type.

The application retains all original document links. A blank notice-page URL does not remove separately supplied document URLs.

### Closing times

CanadaBuys defines its tender closing field using a fixed UTC−05:00 offset. The desk presents the original wall time and offset, its parsed UTC instant, and the local time for the browser.

For example, the original value 2026-10-19T14:00:00 corresponds to 2026-10-19 19:00:00 UTC. The browser's local display follows its own configured zone. The application does not reinterpret that original field using the daylight-saving rules of America/Toronto.

Date-only publication fields remain date-only. A source closing value that cannot be parsed remains visible as supplied.

## 3. Compare complete original editions

Choose **Changes** and select the before and after rows. The original domain compares their complete field values and returns each changed heading with the before and after contents. The desk keeps full descriptions and multiline values in the comparison.

The source-row selector and the comparison selectors identify the retained edition. An updated closing date is a source change; the earlier row remains available. The complete comparison can be opened for its original metadata.

Under **Original source**, download the complete original CSV or the selected full row as JSON. The CSV download checks the returned original byte count and SHA-256 before offering the file. Each source displays the original URL, retrieval time, row count, bytes and digest.

## 4. Record the qualification and delivery fit

**Qualification** is the working review of the specific notice. It has a disposition, owner, next action, note and shortlist selection, plus four substantive planning fields:

| Field | Practical content |
| --- | --- |
| Capability and production scope | The actual engineering, implementation or operational work the team can deliver |
| Eligibility and prime requirements | Source-specific supplier, security, location, language and contracting requirements |
| Commercial route | The potential contracting party, current buying stage and useful partner workshare |
| Calendar and capacity | Published timing beside the required production and partner time |

Add original requirements as individual rows. Each row has its requirement, review state, source or section, and working note. The available states are Unreviewed, Met, Gap to resolve, and Not applicable. These are editable operator decisions.

A new requirement starts with the selected source-row reference when available. Replace or extend it with the relevant original document and section. Keep actual source conditions with the review so the partner can understand what the proposed work depends on.

Press **Save review** to persist the current record. The review uses its own revision. A concurrent change preserves the local draft and shows the newly saved record; the operator can compare the values, apply the draft over that current revision, use the saved version, or download the draft. A read refresh does not silently replace a newer saved workspace with an older response.

## 5. Prepare the whole partner workshare

Open **Workshare** from the selected notice, or **Partner workshares** from the main navigation. Choose **Prepare a workshare**.

The record brings together:

- Named partner or prime, delivery owner and working status.
- Production scope and complete deliverables.
- Partner responsibilities and principal time.
- Original inputs and start conditions.
- Acceptance and operator handover.
- Currency and proposed fee.
- Production hours, partner hours, availability and delivery working days.
- Milestone payment events, amounts, dates or triggers, and acceptance.
- Delivery costs with their planning basis.
- Working notes.

The native server assigns the workshare's stable identifier on its first successful save. The browser then follows that saved identity. The create operation uses the current workspace revision; later edits use that workshare's own saved revision.

Amounts use integer cents. Enter whole amounts or at most two decimal places; the application rejects malformed or out-of-range inputs. Each milestone and cost line remains in the record. The totals show the proposed fee, milestone sum, payment amount still to allocate, entered costs, and fee less those costs.

These totals are calculated from the workshare's entered assumptions. Record labor costing, partner compensation, taxes, timing and expenses explicitly. Different currencies stay separate in the global overview.

The working statuses are Draft, Ready for review, Partner review, Agreed, Delivering, Completed and Passed. Update them to reflect the actual state of the work. The desk preserves the saved record and its history.

### Saved handover

**Download saved handover** fetches the current saved workshare from the native server, then creates a complete standalone HTML handover. It includes all of the commercial and delivery fields, the milestone and cost tables, the original source basis saved with the workshare, current retained notice context and the complete saved workshare JSON. The original basis includes its source edition, row identity and row hash; the current notice remains a separate view of later source changes. It opens without a running server or browser script.

The JSON handover contains the exact returned record. The full original source and the writable application state travel through **Save workspace**.

## 6. Use award and supplier context carefully

The notice detail presents related award and supply-arrangement candidates with their original records and matching evidence. An exact solicitation-number relationship and a suggested commodity crosswalk retain their different evidence.

The original award amount, currency and cumulative value are separate fields. The award source defines contract amount as including taxes. A blank original currency may use the official CAD default; the desk labels the original blank and effective default together.

Cumulative contract value already includes the original contract and amendments. Overlapping complete/fiscal source files and repeated cumulative totals remain original source editions, with the domain's award groups available separately. The desk does not add those cumulative values together.

Instrument type and amendment type are shown when supplied. Original amendment identifiers can contain letters. Supplier names retain their original language. Award date and source retrieval date remain separate because published award data can arrive after the underlying award.

The government GSIN-to-UNSPSC crosswalk is a suggested relationship. Review the instrument scope and the retained match evidence before treating a supplier as a relevant delivery partner.

### Original instrument fields

Award cards show the source supplier legal name, contract number, award date, contract period, instrument and amendment type, and original amendment number alongside the source amount, currency and cumulative contract value. The original strings and full record remain available under **Complete original related record**.

Standing-offer and supply-arrangement cards read the actual 19-column source. Their visible field labels follow the official instrument dictionary:

| Original field | Operator meaning |
| --- | --- |
| agreement-number | Original standing-offer or supply-arrangement identity |
| agreement-type_en / agreement-type_fr | Original agreement type in the selected language |
| supplier-legal-name | Registered supplier name |
| supplier-operating-name | Supplier's business or trading name |
| supplier-standardized-name | Related-name search grouping |
| award-date | Instrument start date |
| expiry-date | Instrument end date |
| date-file-published | Publication date and time of the source file |
| end-user-entity_en / end-user-entity_fr | Entity for whose use the instrument was established |
| delivery-point_en / delivery-point_fr | Original geographic delivery coverage |
| delivery-point-code | Original delivery code |
| commodity | Original commodity code, with its scheme retained as supplied |
| commodity-description_en / commodity-description_fr | Original commodity description |
| sosa-description_en / sosa-description_fr | Original instrument scope |

The standardized name remains a search grouping alongside the legal and operating names. The delivery field preserves its original value; the dictionary also defines FD as Foreign, NA as National–Canada and NC as National Capital. Instrument scope and delivery conditions remain part of the review of a potential supplier relationship.

## 7. Produce reports and receive the saved work

**Reports** downloads HTML, CSV or JSON for all notices, the shortlist, or the selected notice identifiers. It also offers the full portable workspace and saved individual partner handovers.

**Save workspace** preserves the complete current application state and original sources. **Receive workspace** imports that package through the original native receiving operation. Open its returned handoff under **Sources & handoffs** to inspect the preserved source identities and any local review differences.

The operating view reports saved records. Unsaved drafts remain in this browser and have a separate complete draft download. Drafts use browser storage keyed by the actual workspace identity; original source files remain in the native workspace. If browser storage cannot retain a draft, the status asks the operator to download it.

The source and receiving pages retain the complete operation record. Their details can be downloaded as JSON. Received review differences link back to the current notice review when the original notice identifier is available.

## Native browser receiving

OPERATING_JOURNEY.mjs is a reusable operating helper for the real local server and original saved case. The caller supplies a Playwright Page from the existing equipped session, the actual workspace URL, an original notice ID and a private output directory.

The helper can open existing saved review/workshare records, or operate supplied review and workshare edits through the actual browser forms. It downloads the original CSV, complete notice reports, saved workshare handover and portable package. When the original case supplies a receiving URL, the helper receives that same saved package through the receiving application's browser and reopens the same notice/workshare there.

It records actual browser text, download bytes and hashes, screenshots and returned saved identities. It creates no replacement source feed and starts no separate server. Use it in the existing original case, retaining the same application and source edition.

## APM2 original customer case

APM2_OPERATING_CONTENT.mjs provides a complete internal delivery proposal for the retained Shared Services Canada Application Performance Management 2 RFI, solicitation BPM026762/35133. It accepts the original full notice returned by this application's native model and binds each requirement to the actual source edition, row identity, row number and row hash.

The case includes twelve source-linked requirements and full capability, eligibility, commercial and timing notes. Its proposed supplier workshare covers the response master, observability architecture, telemetry and diagnosis, editable capacity and cost model, security information, migration and service operations, supplier evidence register and final handover.

The entered internal proposal is CAD 7,200 across four milestones, with sixty production hours, six partner hours and ten working days from 13–26 October 2026. Entered delivery planning costs total CAD 4,000. These are editable service-planning inputs. The official source facts, its RFI buying stage and its published closing time remain in the same record.

Use the content in the existing original browser case:

~~~js
import { APM2_NOTICE_ID, createApm2OperatingContent }
  from './operator/APM2_OPERATING_CONTENT.mjs';
import { operateCanadaBuysDesk } from './operator/OPERATING_JOURNEY.mjs';

const content = createApm2OperatingContent(
  originalServer.workspace.getNotice(APM2_NOTICE_ID),
  { owner: deliveryOwner, partner: participatingSupplier }
);
const result = await operateCanadaBuysDesk({
  page,
  url: originalServer.url,
  noticeId: content.noticeId,
  review: content.review,
  workshare: content.workshare,
  outputDirectory: originalCaseDirectory,
  receivingUrl: originalReceivingServer.url
});
~~~

The original application must already contain that actual notice. Its existing browser, native model, retained source and receiving installation remain the operating context. An existing saved workshare can instead be supplied as workshareId to continue that same record.

As the original RFI attachment and amendments arrive, extend the requirement register with their actual sections and response fields, then retain the resulting saved workshare edition and partner review.

## Application integration

Serve operator/index.html from the original loopback HTTP service with the same host and origin protections as the native API. The document contains all styles and browser code; it needs no package installation, frontend build or external asset host.

The server's content policy must allow this document's inline script and stylesheet and same-origin API connections. Its source links open ordinary HTTP/HTTPS pages in a separate tab, with no referrer or opener access. Original notice text and raw fields are inserted as text.

The browser calls these original domain routes:

| Operation | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Current saved workspace | GET /api/workspace |
| Full notice and history | GET /api/notices/:id |
| Complete original source | GET /api/sources/:id |
| Original row comparison | GET /api/compare?before=:id&after=:id |
| Original CSV import | POST /api/import |
| Saved review | PATCH /api/notices/:id/review |
| Workshare creation/editing | POST /api/workshares; PATCH /api/workshares/:id |
| Complete saved workshare/history | GET /api/workshares/:id |
| Reports and portable package | GET /api/export; GET /api/package |
| Package receiving | POST /api/receive |
| Original source capture | POST /api/capture |
| Capture and receiving records | GET /api/captures/:id; GET /api/receiving/:packageId |

Report/package scope is all or shortlist; a selected subset sends scope=all with repeated noticeId query parameters. Successful mutations return the complete current workspace. Error responses use error.code, error.message and optional error.details.

The browser never retries a mutation automatically. A failed or uncertain save keeps the working draft available while the original domain's saved state can be refreshed.

## Original source references

- Federal tender open data: https://canadabuys.canada.ca/opendata/pub/openTenderNotice-ouvertAvisAppelOffres.csv
- Current source contract and original government dictionary are retained with this application.
- Government award-source support and 2026 changes: https://donnees-data.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/ba2/ac-cb/COsoutien-CHsupport-eng.html
- Standing offers and supply arrangements: https://sosa.canadabuys.canada.ca/cds/opendata/tpsgc-pwgsc_ocama-sosa.csv
- Supplier instrument dictionary: https://donnees-data.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/ba2/ac-cb/ocama-sosa-dd.xml
- GSIN/UNSPSC mapping catalog: https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/588eab5b-7b16-4a26-b996-23b955965ffa

## Continue the saved case through Applications and merchant tools

`OPERATING_TOOLS.mjs` continues the completed original browser case using its `case-result.json`, original operator and receiving SQLite files, source identity, saved workshare, and prepared merchant publication. It opens the existing operator workspace through the source-owned Applications provider and the registered CanadaBuys MCP provider.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/operator/OPERATING_TOOLS.mjs \
  --source-root /absolute/path/to/merchant-workspace \
  --case-root /absolute/path/to/original-case
```

The source root is the complete maintained checkout. The case root contains the full operating driver's saved `case-result.json`, `operator-workspace/`, and `receiving-workspace/`. Run this continuation after that original case reaches `status: complete`.

The continuation runs the actual registered application command against the existing database, reads its original startup announcement and health response, then closes that command. It loads the declared merchant provider, follows every notice page, reads the saved source and workshare, exports the complete original CSV, and receives every hash-pinned Base64 file chunk. It then follows the original prepared SF30 dataset's cursor through every transport part and reconstructs the whole source/workshare package. Its package digest, complete original CSV and saved workshare are checked against the same customer case.

The output directory contains the actual application startup record and logs, the full CSV delivered through merchant tools, the complete package reconstructed from dataset pages, and `result.json` with source identity, page/chunk counts, preserved workshare, and owned-service closure. The complete source download uses one immutable descriptor. Publication lookup reads its indexed native row directly, keeping file transfers independent of notice-view reconstruction.

For programmatic use, import `operateCanadaBuysTools({sourceDirectory, caseDirectory, outputDirectory})`. The function keeps its output directory on an error and includes that path in `error.operatorToolsDirectory`, so a correction can continue the same saved case.


### Operate the saved desk through the HTTP client

`operator/OPERATING_API.mjs` performs the complete operator workflow through existing CanadaBuysClient instances: it retains the full source CSV and original notice history, saves qualification and partner workshare content with current revisions, downloads all report formats, exports the complete workspace, and receives that exact package into the selected receiving application. Supply the same output directory when explicitly continuing an interrupted operation; the original package and write receipts are retained, and saved workshare identities are reused.

```js
import { CanadaBuysClient } from '../client.mjs';
import { operateCanadaBuysApi } from './OPERATING_API.mjs';

const result = await operateCanadaBuysApi({
  client: new CanadaBuysClient(originalOperatorUrl),
  receivingClient: new CanadaBuysClient(originalReceivingUrl),
  noticeId: retainedNoticeId,
  review: actualQualification,
  workshare: actualPartnerWorkshare,
  outputDirectory: originalOperationDirectory
});

```

Both applications are caller-owned existing workspaces. The result identifies `interface: 'http-api'` and retains the source, review, workshare, reports, complete package and receiving records. A supplied `workshareId` selects a particular saved workshare; otherwise an unambiguous workshare with the same notice, title and partner is reused before creation. Mutation failures are returned with the retained operation directory. The caller can read the existing workspace and deliberately continue the same operation.

`OPERATING_TOOLS.mjs` accepts a completed original customer result with either a browser `browser` journey or an HTTP `operator` journey. It carries the actual interface name into its result, then opens the same SQLite databases through Applications and the registered 37-tool merchant provider.

# Continue the original APM2 procurement customer

This example continues the original CanadaBuys customer created from the complete 908-notice, 67-column federal open-tender capture. It operates the retained APM2 qualification, engineering workshare, reports, receiving workspace and merchant publication. The customer archive and its exact source capture are delivered in the original internal opportunity thread.

The HTTP and browser phases run in separate Node processes so that report/export buffers from the first phase can be released before Chromium starts. Both phases use the same original SQLite workspaces.

## Restore the retained customer

Restore the latest original customer archive with the authorized file service, verify its recorded byte count and SHA256, and retain its original root directory. Preserve these existing members:

- `operator-workspace/workspace.sqlite` and `receiving-workspace/workspace.sqlite`;
- `case-result.json`, `case-input.json` and the complete original open CSV;
- `apm2-operating-content.json`, which contains the source-linked qualification and the internal CAD 7,200 engineering workshare;
- existing `operator-api-journey`, `operator-journey`, `tool-journey` and merchant publication directories.

Materialize the selected complete repository source and original dependency closure under `<customer-root>/source`. Keep the selected source commit and original file hashes with the receiving record. The continuation reads the saved customer; it does not import a fresh substitute feed.

Set `CANADABUYS_CASE_ROOT` to that original customer root. Set `TMPDIR` to a private temporary directory inside it. Use the existing customer operation lock while the programme owns these databases, and keep one receiving owner for this operation.

## Finish the HTTP, merchant and Applications workflow

With Node 24 or a compatible runtime providing `node:sqlite`, run:

```sh
node --max-old-space-size=256 --max-semi-space-size=4 --expose-gc \
  source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/examples/apm2/continue-customer.mjs

node --max-old-space-size=256 --max-semi-space-size=4 --expose-gc \
  source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/operator/OPERATING_TOOLS.mjs \
  --source-root source --case-root "$CANADABUYS_CASE_ROOT"
```

Run these commands from the original customer root, with absolute executable paths where required by the caller's runtime. The first command:

1. Reopens the existing operator and receiving databases and verifies the original source capture.
2. Continues the saved HTTP operation, reconciling its original review, workshare and receiving identities.
3. Downloads complete HTML, CSV and JSON reports and the same full workspace package used by the receiver.
4. Prepares and previews the source-preserving merchant publication.
5. Closes and reopens both SQLite workspaces, retaining the 908 notices, complete original source and saved workshare.

The native API helper checkpoints each write intent and provider result using atomic files. The customer driver records the start and completion of each client call, together with actual process memory. A lost response is reconciled against the saved workshare or content-derived package receipt when the same operation resumes.

The second command loads the actual Applications registration and the registered 37-tool MCP provider, pages the original notice collection, downloads the complete original CSV through retained-file chunks, and reassembles the original merchant payload. Retain its completed `tool-journey/operating-*/result.json`; an already completed result belongs to this customer and should be reused on a later browser continuation.

## Continue the visible browser workflow

After the HTTP customer is complete, use the existing supported Chromium/Headless Shell runtime and Playwright installation. Set `CODEX_PRIMARY_RUNTIME_NODE_MODULES` to the installed module directory. Set `CANADABUYS_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` when the accepted browser is at a different path.

```sh
node --max-old-space-size=256 --max-semi-space-size=4 --expose-gc \
  source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/canadabuys/examples/apm2/continue-browser.mjs
```

This phase opens the original saved workshare through the industrial operator UI, downloads its source, reports and package, and uses the visible receiving form in the same receiving workspace. The existing source-owned `operateCanadaBuysDesk` helper captures the notice, source, qualification, partner-workshare, report and receiving screens. The driver checks the full source hash, receiving review/workshare agreement, original workshare identity, engineering fee and browser errors.

The browser phase retains its own completion or failure in `case-result.json` while preserving the completed HTTP/merchant result. It closes only the browser and servers it started. Actual screenshots remain under the original journey directory, with an inspection copy when the shared workspace can accept one.

## Preserve the completed customer

After each admitted programme ends, preserve the updated original databases, operating records, reports, source bytes, publication and browser captures in the same customer archive. Replace the known artifact version only after reconciling the previous save result. Record the actual executed source commit, phase results and artifact identity in the original internal opportunity thread. Open the resulting browser captures before presenting the visual handoff.
